commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Make reset_cache re-entrant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

A second `reset_cache()` on the offloading connector before the engine steps again fails on `assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush`. The engine keeps running, but the call that made the second reset gets the error. It happens when two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls arrive with no step in between while store jobs are in flight: the first reset moves those jobs into the flush set, which stays set until the next step sends it. In the multiprocess engine, pause and sleep clear caches only once the engine is idle, so they don't hit this; in the in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`), pause clears at once, so a pause or sleep can be one of the two resets. This lets the second reset add to the pending flush set instead of asserting.

The first version of this PR also kept an idle engine stepping until the flush set reached the workers. #62929 now does that (the engine keeps stepping until the flushed jobs are reported), so that part is gone after merging main.

## Claims

- Two `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` calls with no step in between no longer raise. The first reset's flush set still goes out on the next step, and the engine goes idle once the workers report those jobs.
- A single reset is unchanged, and the other three "not in the middle of a step" asserts stay.

## Validation

```
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k reset_twice_before_a_step
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

`test_cache_reset_twice_before_a_step_still_flushes` uses the real-scheduler helpers from #62929: it finishes a request with its store jobs in flight, resets twice, then checks that the next `schedule()` carries exactly those jobs in `jobs_to_flush` and that the engine goes idle once they are reported.

On main (8321d1119bc2, Linux CPU) the second reset fails:

```
>       assert not self._current_batch_jobs_to_flush
E       AssertionError
vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py:2463: AssertionError
```

With the fix it passes, and so does the rest of the file (446 passed, Linux CPU); pre-commit is clean on both files. These tests build the CPU offload region in `/dev/shm`, so they don't run on macOS. No CI step runs this file today: the GPU "V1 KV Connectors" step is disabled, and the CPU step selects only `cpu_test`-marked tests. No GPU run: the reproducer is scheduler-level. Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_reset_cache()` moves every in-flight job id into `_current_batch_jobs_to_flush` and leaves it set on purpose: the workers must wait on those jobs before a later store reuses their CPU chunks, and the set goes out in the next step's metadata. A second reset before that step finds it non-empty. Merging into it is safe: the first reset already moved and cleared every in-flight job, so the second adds no ids, leaves #62929's fence as it is, and does not call `on_reset_flushed()` while the fence is held.

The reset is reached from `pause_generation(clear_cache=True)` and sleep (`EngineCore._reset_caches`, the RL weight-update path), from the dev-mode `POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` and from `LLM.reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)`.

Not a duplicate: #62929 leaves this assert in place, and none of the open offload PRs that touch this file removes it.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview Let an idle P2P-only offload engine report no pending work, using the tier-poll thread introduced in #58168 to service peers. Related context: #51476. ## Claims - P2P reports actual outstanding work instead of keeping the engine busy unconditionally. - The poll thread survives sustained failures, backs off to `max(tier_poll_interval_s, 1 s)`, and rate-limits error reports. ## Validation - `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -s -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/`: **573 passed, 12 skipped**. - Instrumented engine probes verified idle queue parking and the shutdown decision; a deterministic fault probe verified bounded logging, backoff, and recovery. - Ruff 0.14.0 check/format checks, Markdown lint, and `git diff --check` passed. - **Live H100 A/B validation completed:** Qwen3-0.6B, two TP1/DP1 instances, P2P-only, real NIXL transfers over TCP. | Check | Baseline | Fixed | | --- | --- | --- | | Pause, `mode=wait&clear_cache=false` | 4/4 timed out at 10 s | 4/4 HTTP 200 in 22.7–24.7 ms | | Idle EngineCore main-thread context switches/s | 1,014–1,076 | 0 in both 5 s samples | | P2P transfers and matching outputs | 3/3 | 3/3, while source acknowledged paused | | Engine shutdown | Both forced-killed after 15 s | Both normal teardown, container exit 0 | Each arm transferred 1,008 MiB / 576 chunks with zero promotion failures. Outputs also matched across images. This validates the P2P-only path; sleep, DP, multi-tier and RDMA performance were not tested. ## Details Idle polling belongs to the poll thread. Keep the engine stepping when polling is disabled or multiple secondary tiers require scheduler-driven promotions; those configurations retain their existing pause/shutdown limitation. KVCR is unchanged. Rendered documentation describes the supported behavior. Duplicate-work searches found related #61667, #62795, and #62929, which address transfer lifetime, finalization ordering, and cache-reset fencing rather than this idle predicate. Design feedback is welcome. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, and review. ---

commits.pr_title: [MM] Move Nemotron VL image normalization to device
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Move image and video rescaling/normalization for the Nano Nemotron VL models from CPU preprocessing to the model device. This follows the shared GPU-side normalization mechanism introduced in #50411.

Before this change, the processor converted raw `uint8` pixels to `float32` before bicubic interpolation, normalized them on the CPU, and returned pixels in the model dtype. This made resizing more expensive and doubled the amount of pixel data transferred for `bfloat16` models.

This PR:
- opts `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2` into `mm_device_do_normalize`
- keeps resized image and video pixels as `uint8` through preprocessing and transfer (restoring pre-#40283 numerical behavior)
- applies the existing `FusedInputNorm` immediately before the C-RADIO encoder
- handles both fixed-resolution `NCHW` inputs and dynamic-resolution packed patches
- preserves CPU normalization when device normalization is disabled

Bicubic interpolation remains under `torch.compile`. Both normalization modes, with and without resizing, produce one Dynamo graph each with zero graph breaks under the Inductor backend.

### Performance

The renderer and executor are separate processes, so the timings below are
reported per stage and are not added together. Executor work may overlap with
subsequent renderer work.

Setup:

- CPU: Intel Core i9-10920X, one PyTorch intra-op thread
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti
- Model dtype: `bfloat16`
- Reported values: median latency

#### One 1536 x 1536 image

| Stage | Before | After | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer: resize and normalize/prepare pixels | 20.619 ms | **7.161 ms** | **2.88x** |
| Executor: H2D transfer and device normalization | 1.758 ms | **1.255 ms** | **1.40x** |
| Pixel payload | 13.50 MiB | **6.75 MiB** | **2x smaller** |

#### 32 video frames at 512 x 512

| Stage | Before | After | Improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Renderer: resize and normalize/prepare pixels | 50.683 ms | **20.509 ms** | **2.47x** |
| Executor: H2D transfer and device normalization | 6.226 ms | **4.378 ms** | **1.42x** |
| Pixel payload | 48.00 MiB | **24.00 MiB** | **2x smaller** |

## Test Plan

The tests cover:

- retaining `uint8` through compiled bicubic interpolation when device normalization is enabled
- exact `bfloat16` agreement between CPU normalization and `FusedInputNorm`
- both fixed-resolution `NCHW` and dynamic-resolution packed-patch layouts
- CPU-normalized and device-normalized paths for both image and video processors
- rejection of partially enabled rescaling/normalization.


## Test Result

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Skip weight tying for omitted LM heads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Fix initialization of pooling models with quantized token embeddings and `tie_word_embeddings=True`. Packed quantized embeddings have no dense `.weight`, causing initialization to crash when an omitted LM head attempts to tie its weights.


## Claims
- Prevents AttributeError when packed embeddings have no dense .weight.
- Skips weight tying for StageMissingLayer placeholders.
- Adds an end-to-end regression comparing pooled embeddings against a dequantized Transformers reference.


## Validation
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/models/language/pooling/test_embedding.py \
    -k test_pooling_with_tied_quantized_token_embeddings -v
```

Before the fix, initialization fails with: `AttributeError: 'VocabParallelEmbedding' object has no attribute 'weight'`

  After the fix: 1 passed.



## Details
The pooling adapter replaces the unused LM head with `StageMissingLayer`. Previously, the placeholder delegated `tie_weights()` to the original head, which accessed `embed_tokens.weight`. Packed embeddings expose `weight_packed` and `scales` instead.

The placeholder now returns itself from `tie_weights()`.

This fixes omitted heads only. Sequence-classification conversions using `from_2_way_softmax` or `no_post_processing` create a real LM head and still require separate support for extracting dequantized token rows.

Related PRs #45535 and #48870 address quantized embeddings reused by active LM heads. This change specifically handles weight tying delegated through an omitted pooling head.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Reject secondary tiers on engines that span nodes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR makes `TieringOffloadingSpec` fail at startup, instead of serving wrong KV, when secondary tiers run on an engine whose workers span several nodes (#54415).

It applies to `main` on its own and depends on no other PR. #62933 builds on it to support the multiprocessing executor with `--nnodes` > 1.

## Claims

- With secondary tiers and more than one worker, every worker checks at creation whether the engine's workers share a node, and raises `NotImplementedError` if they do not. This covers every way to place workers on several nodes (mp with `--nnodes`, Ray, `external_launcher`) without looking at the executor.
- Single-node engines, single-worker engines and engines without secondary tiers are unchanged.

## Validation

**Multi-node startup** on 2× DGX Spark (GB10), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565` with this branch's changed Python files on top, TP=2, mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, `facebook/opt-125m`:

- `TieringOffloadingSpec` with an `fs` tier: both workers fail at startup with `NotImplementedError: TieringOffloadingSpec secondary tiers are not supported on engines whose workers span several nodes.`
- `TieringOffloadingSpec` without secondary tiers: starts and serves; the same prompt sent twice gives the same output.

**Unit test:** `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py::test_tiering_spec_rejects_secondary_tiers_across_nodes` fakes the TP, PP and PCP groups and `in_the_same_node_as()`: it rejects a TP, PP or PCP group that spans nodes, accepts groups that each share a node, queries all three groups even after one spans nodes, and queries none without secondary tiers. Without the fix, four of its five cases fail. CI provides one host only, so it cannot run a real multi-node rejection.

**Suites** (CPU-only container):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector
# 1286 passed, 1 failed (on 71294c2e9a)
```

The one failure, `test_worker.py::test_register_packed_kv_caches_skips_scratch_group`, needs a GPU and fails the same way on `main`; it passes on GPU.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** The tiering scheduler and its secondary tiers run in the engine core and address only its node's `/dev/shm` region. Since #58497 every worker writes the slot of its rank, but workers on other nodes write it into their own node's region. Secondary tiers therefore persist rows without those slots, and promotions never fill them.

**Detection.** An engine's workers form a grid of its TP, PP and PCP groups (DCP lives inside TP), so they all share one node exactly when each of those groups does. `create_worker()` therefore calls `in_the_same_node_as()` on each group with more than one rank. It is a collective over that group, which every worker of the group reaches during KV cache registration. Every rank runs all three before any of them raises, so a rank whose own TP group spans nodes cannot leave the ranks of a node-local TP group waiting in the PP or PCP collective. It runs only with secondary tiers, since without them each node's region serves its own workers.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for "54415 in:body", "multi-node offload", "secondary tiers nodes", "local_world_size offload" and "shared region node". #53474 also sizes node-local regions and rejects multi-node secondary tiers from the config; #46556 moves rank-local shards to a shared filesystem through worker transfers instead; #62058 and #53073 deal with `/dev/shm` capacity and region lifecycle, not with nodes.

**Docs:** `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md` states the restriction.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Add nixl auto-label rule and assign topic owners
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a `nixl` auto-label rule to `.github/mergify.yml`, mirroring the existing `mooncake` rule ([#59192](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59192)). PRs touching NIXL-related files or KV-offloading paths — the multi-tiered offloading path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/`, KVCR tiering) and the NIXL KV connector (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/`, `vllm/distributed/nixl_utils.py`) — are labeled `nixl` and assigned to @ovidiusm and @iyastreb, so the NIXL team gets notified of KVCR / connector changes.

The `nixl` GitHub label itself is created out-of-band (labels are not versioned in this repo, and mergify cannot add a label that does not exist).

## Claims

- PRs touching any path containing `nixl` (case-insensitive) get the `nixl` label. This covers the NIXL KV connector and `vllm/distributed/nixl_utils.py`, NIXL EP dispatch (`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/nixl_ep.py`), EC-transfer NIXL data (`vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/data/nixl.py`), the NIXL p2p data layer of the multi-tiered offload path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py`), and all NIXL tests, design docs, examples and tools.
- PRs touching any path containing `kv_offload` get the `nixl` label. This covers the multi-tiered offloading path (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/`, KVCR tiering), the simple offload path (`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/`), their tests, and `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`.
- PRs with "NIXL" in the title get the `nixl` label.
- Matching PRs are assigned to @ovidiusm and @iyastreb (the assignment is what notifies them).

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml` — all hooks pass, including `check-label-rules` (every `files=`/`files~=` condition matches at least one tracked file).
- Verified the two regexes against `git ls-files`: 155 tracked files match, all of them NIXL or KV-offloading related; negatives (e.g. `gpu_model_runner.py`, mooncake connector/tests, `offloading_connector.py`) correctly do not match; all paths covered by the original hardcoded list are still covered (strict superset).
- `gh label list --repo vllm-project/vllm` — confirms the `nixl` label exists.
- Duplicate checks: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "nixl label"` and `--search "auto-label"` — no open PR adds a nixl auto-label rule.
- No model evaluations: mergify/CI configuration only, no serving, output, or accuracy impact.

## Details

- The file conditions use `files~=(?i)nixl` and `files~=kv_offload` (per @hmellor's review suggestion) instead of a hardcoded directory list, matching the style of the existing `kimi`/`rust` rules. A path regex survives files moving between directories; the `check-label-rules` pre-commit hook exists precisely because hardcoded paths silently rot.
- Scope note: the `kv_offload` substring intentionally also covers `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/`, and `(?i)nixl` covers NIXL EP dispatch and EC-transfer NIXL files — all NIXL / KV-offloading work the team wants to be notified of.
- The rule follows the `label-mooncake` pattern exactly: label add + `assign` to the topic owners.
- This is not duplicating an existing PR: no open PR adds a nixl label rule (see duplicate checks above), and the existing `label-kv-connector` rule only adds the generic `kv-connector` label without assigning or notifying NIXL owners.
- AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR (Mistral Vibe). The diff is a small addition to `.github/mergify.yml`.

commits.pr_title: [Docs] Add Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B recipe
[Bugfix][KV Offload] Pin a shared-prefix junction when a sparse group cuts the offload hit
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Fixes #63565. On hybrid models with sparse retention (the default), a prefix that lives only in the CPU offload tier is never reused by a request that diverges before the single stored Mamba/sliding-window state. The offload lookup now pins a shared-prefix junction there, as the local prefix cache already does, so the prefix heals after one miss. ## Claims - A revisit that shares a prefix but diverges inside the prompt's last block hits the offload tier from the second revisit on (today: never). - No change when every group hits, when no full-attention group proves a hit, under dense retention (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=None`), or for models without a sliding-window/Mamba group. - A junction set by the local prefix cache is never lowered. ## Validation CPU (x86, torch 2.14.0+cpu, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k junction # main: test_sparse_group_miss_registers_shared_prefix_junction FAILED assert 0 == 16; 2 passed # this PR: 3 passed pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_offload \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py # this PR: 86 failed / 1,740 passed / 24 skipped (the same 86 fail on main) ``` The 86 failures are the same on main and are environmental on a CPU-only host: 32 in `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py` (copies through a GPU) and 54 EC-connector cases in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` (a multimodal model config is not available there). `pre-commit run --files `: all hooks pass. GPU (4 × Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.14.0+xpu, vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.15.4): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B BF16, TP 4, `--enforce-eager --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 16 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048`, 576-token blocks, GPU KV cache capped at 66K tokens (`--kv-cache-memory`) so that filler requests evict the documents from the GPU prefix cache. Serial requests. Six ~16.1K-token documents, three whose question starts inside the block that holds the stored GDN state (in-band) and three whose question starts after it (out-of-band); each is read with question A, then revisited with question B and question C, with six 16K-token fillers before each revisit. GPU prefix-cache hits were 0 on every revisit. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | in-band, revisit B | 0/3 offload hits, TTFT 1.49 s | 0/3, TTFT 1.49 s (one more GDN state stored: 0.15 vs 0.09 GB) | | in-band, revisit C | 0/3, TTFT 1.50 s | 3/3, 15,552 of ~16,140 tokens from the offload tier, TTFT 0.30 s | | out-of-band, B and C | 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3 | Same documents and questions in both runs (fixed seed). The greedy answers of the three healed in-band hits equal main's answers to the same prompts, which main computed without a hit. ## Details Under sparse retention each request keeps one sparse-group checkpoint, in the last block of its prompt. A later request that shares the prefix but diverges before that block finds its full-attention chunks in the offload tier but no Mamba state at or below them, so `_lookup_complete_chunks` returns 0 for the whole request. The local prefix cache handles the same geometry by returning a shared-prefix junction from `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` (`kv_cache_manager.py:318-326`); the recompute then retains the sparse state there. The offload lookup never set one, so once the prefix had left the GPU cache every recompute stored its state inside the differing suffix again. Change (`offloading/scheduler.py`): - `_lookup_complete_chunks` records, in `RequestOffloadState.full_attention_hit_boundary`, the boundary the full-attention groups proved before the first sliding-window/Mamba group narrowed it (not on a deferred lookup). - `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, when the final hit is shorter than that boundary and retention is sparse, raises `request.shared_prefix_boundary` to it. No core change is needed: the scheduler sets the local junction before it calls the connector (`sched/scheduler.py:1077-1089`), and everything downstream reads the request field: the align split stops a chunk there (`sched/scheduler.py:610`), `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` retains it (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:511-518`), and the aligned-boundary hand-off stores it to the offload tier. Limits: the first revisit still misses (a first-visit hit needs a state retained below the replay boundary, which is the subject of #57613). Connectors that set `hit_diverged` and load nothing re-read the local junction (`sched/scheduler.py:1162-1172`) and can overwrite this one; the plain `OffloadingConnector` does not take that path. If #62278 (junction as a tuple of positions) merges first, this needs a small rebase to add the junction to `shared_prefix_boundaries`. Why this is not a duplicate: searched on 2026-10-24 for "shared_prefix_boundary", "junction", "offload shared_prefix_boundary", "offloading mamba junction" and "OffloadingConnector hybrid". #45238 is the GPU-cache form of this geometry (main has the GPU junction, #47782 / #37898); #57613 retains a block below sliding-window replay boundaries (first visit, different mechanism); #59146 keeps the prompt-end checkpoint; #56795 is a different offload-store bug; #52774 backfills GPU-local divergent hits only; #62400 adds junctions to the MooncakeStore connector; #63221 changes the connector load boundary under EAGLE. None sets a junction from the `OffloadingConnector` lookup. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write the change and the tests, and draft this text. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][OBJ] Don't lose a completed transfer when telemetry is unavailable
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

In `obj/manager.py`, `_poll_active_transfers` calls `get_xfer_telemetry()` after the transfer completed, and the call sits outside any `try`. Builds compiled without telemetry raise there. The exception escapes the tier, so a finished job is lost.

This is the same defect as #63787 at a different call site. In the connector an enclosing `except Exception` catches the raise and reports a false failure. Here nothing catches it.

## Change

Guard the call. On a raise, log once and leave `transfer_time` as `None`. The job still reports success and the handle is still released. Only the timing is lost. Nothing changes when telemetry works.

## Tests

`test_telemetry_failure_does_not_lose_successful_transfer`: a raising `get_xfer_telemetry` must still give `JobResult(success=True)` with `transfer_time is None`. Without the guard this test does not pass, so it pins the bug. It sits next to `test_post_transfer_cleanup_failure_does_not_lose_result` and `test_release_xfer_failure_retries_without_losing_result`, which cover the same shape for the other cleanup calls.

It passes on the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image with this branch on `main` at `4f140a2`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass on both files.

## Scope

I did not reproduce this one in a live deployment, because we do not run the OBJ tier. It is the same bug shape at a call site with less protection. I found it while I fixed the connector.

## Relationship to #62650

#62650 covers a failed NIXL submission in the same file. This covers a telemetry raise after the transfer completed. Different functions, no shared code.

I applied both to current `main` in both orders. There is no conflict in `obj/manager.py` or `test_obj_tier.py`. Whichever lands first, the other needs no change. I can rebase on #62650 if that is easier to review.

I also ran the tiering tests with #62650 applied on top of this branch. The result is the same as with #62650 alone, so the two changes do not interfere.

## Note

Split out of #58038 for @orozery. The NIXL connector half is #63787.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream DeepSeek V4/V3.2 string tool arguments incrementally
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52846.

DeepSeek V4, V4.1 and V3.2 streamed a long string tool argument as one fragment when `</｜DSML｜parameter>` arrived. The configs set `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")`, so the engine skipped every plain body delta.

The fix now uses the per-parser `arg_value_extender` hook, the same way GLM (#61253) and Gemma4 (#61494) do. The earlier engine-level gate change is dropped.

- `vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py`: `_dsml_arg_value_extender` returns an extender while the last parameter is an open `string="true"` value. Each delta streams as escaped JSON text without rerunning the converter. It stops on a parameter tag, keeping a tail so a tag split across deltas is caught.
- Wired into `deepseek_v4_config`, `deepseek_v32_config`, and `deepseek_v41_config` (spaced DSML tags via `functools.partial`).
- `_param_patterns`: the trailing-partial regex holds back an unfinished next `<｜DSML｜parameter` tag, so a streamed value never includes it (implicit close case).

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py`: `test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental` (4096-char body in 32-char chunks, needs >1 non-empty body delta and exact round-trip), `test_streaming_non_string_argument_is_withheld_until_close`, `test_streaming_string_argument_with_markup_is_incremental`.
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::TestExtractToolCallsStreaming::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close`
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close` (spaced DSML)
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py::TestArgValueExtender` (split close tag, closed value, non-string value, repeated key)

Commands (CPU only):

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py

pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v41.py

pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers --ignore=tests/parser/cohere

ruff check <changed files>; ruff format --check <changed files>
```

## Test Result

On this branch:

```text
deepseek v3/v31/v32/v4 tool parsers:  82 passed, 1 xfailed
engine + glm47 + gemma4 + v41 set:     589 passed
tests/parser + tests/tool_parsers:     7672 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed, 41 errors
ruff: All checks passed! / 6 files already formatted
```

The 41 errors are setup errors in `test_harmony.py` and `test_llama3_json_tool_parser.py` (gated or unreachable HF downloads on my machine). `tests/parser/cohere` was skipped: `cohere_melody` is not installed.

Same new tests against upstream/main parser code:

```text
FAILED test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py::test_streaming_long_string_argument_is_incremental - assert 0 > 1
FAILED test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py::...::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 0 > 1
FAILED parser/engine/test_deepseek_v41.py::test_long_string_argument_streams_before_close - assert 2 > (4096 // 64)
```

V4, 4096-char body in 128 chunks: 0/128 body chunks emit arguments on main, 128/128 on this branch.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
commits.pr_body:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

## Throughput results

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`
- 18 batch sizes from `B = 1` through `B = 256`
- Prefix lengths `S = 512, 8192, 32768`

The table reports decode throughput for adaptive verification relative to fixed verification at the same maximum depth. Each value is the unweighted mean over the `(B, S)` at that speculative depth.

| Maximum depth | Adaptive / fixed at same depth |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.965× |
| 2 | 0.958× |
| 3 | 0.965× |
| 4 | 1.065× |
| 5 | 1.127× |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fault a peer whose source WRITE stalls
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Part of #63602 (gap 2, source half). Builds on #64250 (merged), which retains the stalled transfer across the teardown this fault triggers. One commit on main (`ffaa825b33`).

A source WRITE that NIXL keeps reporting as `PROC`/`PEND` past `VLLM_P2P_TRANSFER_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` (default 20 s) now faults its peer. The fault releases nothing.

## Claims

- A stalled source transfer faults its peer and ends the session. Before this change, nothing ever faulted it, and `write_blocks()` kept posting new WRITEs to the wedged peer.
- The fault releases nothing. The stalled transfer and its pins are retained across teardown (#64250) until the transport reports it stopped.
- A stall fault skips the 10 s peer-fault drain, since a stalled transfer would never drain.

## Validation

The issue's source-side property: a WRITE still pending at 300 s must have faulted its peer, while keeping the transfer and its store job held.

```
main (with #64250): consumer_failed_at_s=35.0; source_alive=True;  inflight=[0]; pinned=[1]; peer_fault=None                    -> FAILED
this PR:            consumer_failed_at_s=35.0; source_alive=False; inflight=[0]; pinned=[1]; peer_fault=transfer stalled for 20s -> PASSED
```

The issue body's `test_gap2_pending_transfer.py` still fails, for an unrelated reason. It hard-codes the consumer failing at exactly 40 s, but since #63781 the consumer fails at 35 s (30 s load + 5 s abort-ack). The check above is the same scenario without that hard-coded timing.

New tests, run with this PR's tests on #64250's code:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py -k stall
FAILED ...::test_stalled_transfer_faults_peer_without_releasing   E  assert not True
FAILED ...::test_stalled_peer_gets_no_new_writes                  E  assert None is not None
2 failed, 2 passed
```

(The two that pass guard the no-fault cases: under the deadline, and the deadline disabled with 0.)

With this PR:

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.../nvidia/cu13/lib pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p
426 passed
$ pre-commit run --files <changed>      # mypy included
Passed
```

CPU-only, and CI runs it in `misc.yaml`. **The 20 s default is not yet measured on GPU.** It is far above the ~131 ms p99 tiering-lock hold we measured on H200 at c256, and above healthy transfer times seen so far. Before this leaves draft, I'd like to measure transfer duration by size under load from NIXL telemetry, and run a real stall (`rc_gda` re-enabled, as in #63499).

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `NixlTransport.poll()` treats `PROC`/`PEND` as "wait" forever.
- `_drain_abort` holds a stuck transfer and its AbortAck forever, and only logs after 10 s.
- Nothing records when a transfer was submitted, so nothing faults the peer.
- `write_blocks` is gated only on `peer_fault`, so the source keeps feeding the wedged peer.

In the GPU run in #63602, 36 WRITEs never completed, and pulls from a *healthy* peer dropped (679/847).

**Change.**
- `_InflightXfer.submitted_at` is set on submit.
- `ServerRole.collect_results()` checks for stalls when the transport reports no fault. Once the oldest in-flight transfer is past the timeout, it sets `peer_fault = "transfer stalled for Ns"` and `transfer_stalled`.
- Everything after that is the existing #60374 path: no new WRITEs, `_escalate_peer_fault` then `DisconnectMsg` (the consumer fails its loads), reap, and the data-plane reconnect backoff.
- `_escalate_peer_fault` skips its drain wait when `transfer_stalled` is set.

Detection lives in `ServerRole`, not `NixlTransport`. It sits next to the `_STORE_TIMEOUT_S` logic it mirrors, it doesn't depend on which transport is used, and the session reproducers exercise it directly.

**Why it depends on #64250.** Without retention, the teardown this fault triggers would run `cancel(mode="immediate")` and unpin the stalled transfer's blocks. That is the very release the deadline must not cause.

**New env var** `VLLM_P2P_TRANSFER_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` is a float, default 20, and 0 disables it. It is documented in `vllm/envs.py` and in the P2P table in `docs/usage/security.md`, next to the other `VLLM_P2P_*` limits.

Complexity: about 40 non-test lines.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Offload] Avoid repeated hash-prefix scans
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Avoid repeated scans of previously processed request hashes when `OffloadingConnector` updates offload keys. Preserve key order, chunk boundaries, and recorded token positions.

## Claims

- Each update reads only the newly selected hashes, instead of traversing the existing prefix again for each cache group.
- Updates with no complete new chunk avoid scanning old hashes.
- The regression test checks incremental updates, incomplete chunks, repeated calls, multiple chunk sizes, key order, and token positions.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.13, the five focused tests below passed on this rebased change. All applicable hooks passed.

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  --noconftest -q \
  -k 'update_offload_keys_without_scanning_hash_prefix or normal_store_excludes_align_mode_mamba_sources or partial_lookup_returns_exact_boundary_and_group_load_keys or recurrent_group_unhashed_block_does_not_truncate_load_boundary or partial_lookup_requires_every_cache_group'

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

These are CPU tests with mocked scheduler inputs. `--noconftest` excludes unrelated GPU fixtures. Buildkite already includes this test file in the V1 KV Connectors suite.

The regression uses a hash list that rejects iteration but permits indexed access. Restoring the method from main (`8fb16ea5a66f0ef362e728f0ff025f2845927fd5`) in memory makes the test fail. The rebased method passes. This establishes the traversal change without a timing threshold.

End-to-end serving and model evaluation remain pending for this rebased commit. No model, GPU, workload, or serving speedup is claimed. Human review of every changed line and the required serving validation remain pending.

## Details

Without this change, `RequestOffloadState.update_offload_keys()` uses `islice` to skip hashes that already have offload keys. Skipping still consumes the iterator from the beginning. Every call therefore traverses the hash list again, even when the request has no new complete chunk.

This method runs during offload lookup, scheduler updates, and request completion. The repeated CPU work grows with the request hash count and affected requests. It adds work to the scheduler path. The effect on serving latency and throughput is not measured here.

`Request.block_hashes` is a list. Indexed slicing starts at the next unprocessed chunk boundary and selects each chunk's final hash. Key construction and position updates remain unchanged. The temporary list contains only newly selected hashes, at the cost of one short-lived list per group per update.

Open-PR searches for `update_offload_keys` and `offload hash` found no duplicate of this traversal fix. Related #54743 changes which cache groups support offloading. It does not remove this repeated hash-prefix traversal.

AI assistance was used to prepare, review, and test this change.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Qwen3.5 GDN: overlap in_proj_ba with in_proj_qkvz on the aux stream
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA path (no torch.compile, #51012), run the tiny `in_proj_ba` GEMM on the aux stream so it hides behind `in_proj_qkvz`.
- It engages only during CUDA graph capture, for ≤ 256 tokens, and only when `in_proj_ba` is an unquantized cuBLAS GEMM;
- the threshold is hard-coded from a sweep across model sizes, quant formats and TP sizes. 

## Claims

- **Decode TPOT −2.7% / −2.2%** (C=1 / C=16) on `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` TP1
- **Decode TPOT −4.4% / −2.6%** (C=1 / C=16) on `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` TP4.
- **Outputs bitwise identical** to the serial path.

## Validation

### E2E

TPOT (ms), mean of 2 rounds; same GPUs, A B A B, shared FlashInfer autotune cache, `vllm bench serve` random dataset with `--ignore-eos`. Base = this branch with the threshold set to 0. Round-to-round spread ≤ 1.3% at C ≤ 16, ≤ 1.5% at C=64. On 397B-NVFP4 (BF16 `linear_attn`) the overlap engages in every layer.

| Workload | 27B-NVFP4 TP1: base → PR | Δ | 35B-A3B TP2: base → PR | Δ | 397B-A17B-NVFP4 TP4: base → PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1k/512, C=1 | 5.358 → 5.215 | −2.7% | 2.613 → 2.535 | −3.0% | 4.380 → 4.188 | −4.4% |
| 1k/512, C=16 | 6.876 → 6.722 | −2.2% | 4.677 → 4.520 | −3.4% | 7.353 → 7.158 | −2.6% |
| 1k/512, C=64 | 11.491 → 11.380 | −1.0% | 7.389 → 7.361 | −0.4% | 12.201 → 12.006 | −1.6% |
| 8k/1k, C=64 | 21.429 → 21.300 | −0.6% | 9.532 → 9.476 | −0.6% | 16.384 → 16.235 | −0.9% |

### Correctness

- **Gate:** building the layer from the configs of 12 checkpoints (BF16, FP8, GPTQ, NVFP4 V1/V2, Qwen3.6 NVFP4, 2.4T BF16/FP8/NVFP4) enables the overlap on all but `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` (FP8 `in_proj_ba`), and on none with `--linear-backend flashinfer_cutedsl`.
- **Why the gate:** overlapping two FP8 per-tensor projections (2.4T per-rank shapes, autotuned FlashInfer `bmm_fp8`, CUDA graph) gives wrong outputs: 172/6400 and 432/6400 mismatching outputs at TP8, M = 1 and 8 (also with forced cuBLAS/cuDNN tactics; CUTLASS was clean). `bmm_fp8` runs every call on one process-wide workspace.
- **Tests:** `pytest tests/models/test_qwen3_5.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py`: 20 passed. No new test: the change only moves an unchanged GEMM onto another stream inside graph capture, which the bitwise check covers.
- **Eval:** GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, temperature 0, full set) on the PR arm with Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4: 0.964, no invalid responses.

### Choosing the threshold

One CUDA graph replays 8–64 distinct layers (> 512 MB of weights, HBM-cold); median of 3 fresh processes; M = 1..8192 (the 21 rows added for large models and the remaining formats: M = 1..513) including every capture size from 128 to 512. Serial-vs-serial noise: median 0.01%, p95 0.7%.

- **≤ 256 tokens:** the overlap wins or ties everywhere (worst −0.01 µs/layer); typical savings 2–5 µs/layer, 2–3 µs on Qwen3.8-2.4T (TP4–16).
- **First regression:** 27B BF16 TP8 at 272 tokens (+3.7 µs), a cuBLAS kernel switch rather than a gradual crossover; that setup still saves 2.2 µs at 256. 272 is the next capture size, so 256 is the largest threshold that is safe everywhere. Next regressions: 27B FP8 block TP8 at 464, 35B-A3B TP4 at ~1024.

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint coverage (which formats engage, which rows cover them)</summary>

| Checkpoints | qkvz / ba | Overlap | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen official BF16 (Qwen3.5 0.8B–397B, Qwen3.6 27B/35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B) | BF16 / BF16 | yes | BF16 rows (Qwen3.6 has the Qwen3.8-27B / Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shapes) |
| Qwen official FP8 (Qwen3.5 27B/35B/122B/397B, Qwen3.6 27B/35B, Qwen3.8-27B) | FP8 block / BF16 | yes | FP8 block rows |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8` (linear_attn not converted) | BF16 / BF16 | yes | 2.4T rows |
| Qwen official GPTQ-Int4 (27B, 35B-A3B, 122B, 397B; linear_attn unquantized) | BF16 / BF16, ba replicated (N = 2·heads at every TP) | yes | GPTQ rows |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, `Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4`, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`, `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2` | FP8 per-tensor / BF16 | yes | FP8 per-tensor rows |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4`, `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4` | BF16 / BF16 | yes | NVFP4 ckpt (BF16) rows |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` | FP8 per-tensor / FP8 per-tensor | no (serial) | — |
| Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4-Exp) | — | not opted in | — |

</details>

## Details

**Design**

- **Opt-in per caller** (`overlap_ba_proj=True`): only the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA path, which never runs under torch.compile, enables it. A compiled caller would need a custom op or Dynamo's stream tracing. Also off with micro-batching (its threads would share the layer's events) and LoRA (not validated on the aux stream).
- **Only when `in_proj_ba` is a plain cuBLAS GEMM** (`UnquantizedLinearMethod` with the default torch GEMM), checked at init. torch's cuBLAS workspace is per handle and stream, so it cannot collide with whatever kernel runs `in_proj_qkvz` (cuBLAS, FlashInfer `bmm_fp8`/`mm_mxfp8`, CUTLASS block FP8 with a per-call allocator workspace). FlashInfer GEMMs instead share one process-wide workspace per op (`bmm_fp8_workspace`, `mm_bf16_workspace`), so a quantized `ba` (FP8 in `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4`, where both projections run `bmm_fp8`) or `--linear-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` (`mm_bf16`'s cuBLASLt path above 32 tokens) keeps the serial path. Same restriction as Kimi K3's side-stream path.
- **Only under CUDA graph capture.** Eagerly, the stream switch and events cost ~40 µs of host time per layer, more than the overlap saves.
- **Hard-coded threshold, no env switch**

**Alternatives considered**

- **Merge `in_proj_ba` into `in_proj_qkvz`** (one GEMM; #41457 does this as a 6-way `in_proj`). Both read the same input, but a merge needs the same quant scheme and the same TP sharding:
  - `in_proj_ba` is BF16 in every FP8, GPTQ and NVFP4 Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 checkpoint except `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` (FP8 per-tensor, like its qkvz), while `in_proj_qkvz` is BF16, FP8 per-tensor, FP8 block or MXFP8. Merging would mean quantizing `ba` (a numerics change to the gating inputs) or keeping two GEMMs anyway.
- **#56534** (draft, same idea, different scope): when both projections are static per-tensor FP8 with equal input scales, it quantizes the input once and runs the two FP8 GEMMs concurrently in a custom op. It targets checkpoints like `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4`, more complex, out of scope for and complementary to this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Compile] Fix KV-cache corruption under whole-graph compile (revert #42129)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implements solution 2 as outlined in issue #62865.
In more detail: fixes #62865 by reverting #42129 and, under torch < 2.13, keeps its intended hang protection by not formatting the slow log message for vLLM ops.
Currently using compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []` on Transformers-backend models corrupts the KV cache because Inductor passes tensors in a different layout than the kernels assume. As discussed with maintainers and @okorzh-amd (author of #42129) in Slack, this is the revert-based alternative to #62924.

## Claims

- Fixes degenerate output for Transformers-backend models (e.g. Qwen3, Kolibri-1, likely others) under compile mode 1/2, or mode 3 with `splitting_ops: []`.
- It does so by restoring PyTorch's default handling for all `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` custom ops.
- Keeps the compile-hang protection from #42129 through: (1) from torch 2.13 the slow log message is only built with INFO logging; (2) below 2.13 (currently only the gfx1250 preview image) the message is never built for `vllm::` and `vllm_aiter::` ops, the same ops #42129 covered.

## Validation

Environment: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, torch 2.13.0+cu130, precompiled kernels. All runs with vLLM and Inductor compile caches disabled.

### Correctness
**1. Regression test** 
Added a new test `test_whole_graph_compile` which uses Qwen3-0.6B on the Transformers backend on compile mode 2 vs eager with `check_logprobs_close`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_whole_graph_compile -v
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` | failed: `Matched tokens: []`, ref `'LLM is a large language model, ...'`, test `'>>1\n\n\n\n...'` |
| this PR | passed 2 runs|

**2. GSM8K** 
With this PR, mode 2 matches eager and the native implementation on GSM8K (Qwen3-0.6B, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`); while on main there is a clear regression.

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|
| Transformers backend, eager | 0.391 | 0.3% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, `main` | 0.011 | 10.8% |
| Transformers backend, mode 2, this PR | 0.401 | 0.2% |
| native vLLM implementation, default mode 3 | 0.400 | 0.2% |

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers --max-model-len 4096 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode": 2, "backend": "inductor", "cudagraph_mode": 2}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

**3. Bounded log message for vLLM ops under torch < 2.13**
Introduced a test `tests/compile/test_inductor_operator_str_patch.py` which checks that a `vllm::` op's message is only its name. Running on torch 2.12 (CPU, a small compiled graph with a `vllm::` op and a custom op from another namespace), unpatched torch builds the full message for both ops; with the patch it is never built for the `vllm::` op. 
I could not test on gfx1250 itself.

### Compile time
On CUDA, cold-cache compile time is unchanged within noise (`main` vs this PR): Kolibri-1 mode 3 28.3 vs 28.1 s, Kolibri-1 TP=2 61.1 vs 62.1 s, Qwen3-4B mode 3 19.4 vs 19.5 s.

On ROCm, @djramic reported on Slack that without the #42129 allow-list the Kimi-K2 arch (dummy weights, torch 2.13) compiles about as fast as before. I had no ROCm access to verify this myself.

## Details

**Root cause:** #42129 added every `vllm::*` and `vllm_aiter::*` op to Inductor's `FALLBACK_ALLOW_LIST`. Inductor creates fallbacks for allow-listed ops without PyTorch's default layout constraint for custom ops. Without it, Inductor passes `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` a head-major key, strides `(128, 128*S, 1)` instead of eager's `(1024, 128, 1)`. `reshape_and_cache_flash` only reads `key.stride(0)` and assumes packed heads, so every cached key is scrambled and the output is garbage. Default mode 3 is unaffected because it splits the graph at the attention and KV-cache ops.

**Why revert:** The allow-list only existed to skip an implicit-fallback INFO message that torch <= 2.12 builds eagerly, which hung compilation on deep MoE/TP graphs. pytorch/pytorch#185951 makes it lazy from torch 2.13, and CUDA, CPU, XPU and the default ROCm images are on >= 2.13. Reverting restores PyTorch's behavior for all vLLM ops. #62924's own control row (allow-list disabled) already gives token-identical output to its patched run. The allow-list cannot stay for torch < 2.13 either, because the layout bug is in that code path on every torch version; those versions only need the hang protection, which skipping the message for vLLM ops provides.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- The torch < 2.13 patch can be removed once every platform pins torch >= 2.13. Until then, Inductor messages for vLLM ops (including lowering errors) show only the op name on those versions, as with #42129.
- On torch >= 2.13 with Inductor's graph logger at INFO, the full message is still built and can be slow on very deep graphs (`IRNode.__str__` has no depth limit, as #43111 found). This is opt-in debug logging.
- Overlaps with #57310, whose allow-list change should become unnecessary.
- A follow-up PR could make the KV-cache writers (reshape_and_cache, reshape_and_cache_flash and their Triton versions) reject keys whose heads are not packed, so a future layout change raises an error instead of silently corrupting the cache.

## Overview

Lets `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` checkpoints (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL) run without `--trust-remote-code` on transformers ≥ 5.18.

Related to #63470. Alternative to #64030 (see Details).

## Claims

- `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-*` serves without `--trust-remote-code` when transformers ≥ 5.18 is installed.
- `--trust-remote-code`, older transformers versions, and the existing Nano VL / Nano Omni checkpoints behave as before.
- CI now initializes the model from transformers' built-in `nemotron_h_omni` config.
- `supported_models.md` lists the architecture and the transformers ≥ 5.18 requirement for running without the flag.

## Details

**Root cause.** Transformers 5.18 added a built-in `nemotron_h_omni` config. The Super VL checkpoints declare `"model_type": "nemotron_h_omni"`, so `AutoConfig` loads that class without remote code. The built-in class renames `vit_hidden_size` to `vision_hidden_size`, but `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2.__init__` read `config.vit_hidden_size`.

**Fix.** Read `vision_hidden_size`, the name the built-in transformers config uses, and fall back to `vit_hidden_size`, which the remote-code configs use:

| Config | Field |
|---|---|
| Transformers built-in `nemotron_h_omni` (≥ 5.18) | `vision_hidden_size` |
| Checkpoint remote code (`--trust-remote-code`) | `vit_hidden_size` |
| Nano VL / Nano Omni checkpoints | `vit_hidden_size` |

**Test.** The `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` registry entry was an offline placeholder. It now points at `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16` without `trust_remote_code`, gated on transformers ≥ 5.18.0. The built-in `NemotronHConfig` derives `hybrid_override_pattern` from `layers_block_type` and doesn't allow setting it, so the 2-layer override sets `layers_block_type` instead. The "Basic Models (Extra Initialization)" CI step selects this test.

**Why not #64030.** #64030 copies the remote-code config and image processor into vLLM, about 520 lines. Transformers ≥ 5.18 already provides the config, and serving goes through `NanoNemotronVLProcessor` either way, so vLLM only needs this one field read. This matches #60623, which removed configs vLLM had copied once Transformers shipped them.

**Limitations.**
- **Older transformers:** on transformers < 5.18, `--trust-remote-code` is still required.
- **Audio:** the built-in config also renames `sound_config` → `audio_config`, which vLLM doesn't read. The Super VL checkpoints have no audio, but a future checkpoint that loads with the built-in config and includes audio would have audio switched off with no error. Left for a follow-up.
- **Recipe:** the Super VL recipe keeps `--trust-remote-code` until a release includes this fix. Its pinned image (v0.31.0) doesn't have it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not offload the partially computed block of a request that finished with an error
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

When a request finishes with an error before its prefill is complete, the block it was computing is stored under the hash of the full block. A later request with that prefix hits the offloaded block and loads KV for tokens that were never computed. One-expression fix in `_build_store_jobs`; sibling of #59096 and #59329.

## Claims

- A request that ends in `FINISHED_ERROR` mid-prefill stores only the blocks it fully computed, as `FINISHED_ABORTED` already does.
- Requests that finished normally are unchanged: they computed their whole prompt, so the clamp is a no-op.

## Validation

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q -k finish_mid_prefill
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
```

`test_finish_mid_prefill_stores_only_computed_blocks[FINISHED_ERROR|FINISHED_ABORTED]` runs a 16-token prompt through chunked prefill at 6 tokens a step (block size 4), finishes the request after the first chunk, and checks that the finish step stores nothing beyond the one full block step 1 already stored.

On main (<SHA>) the `FINISHED_ERROR` case fails:

```
AssertionError: FINISHED_ERROR: stored 1 blocks [2] but only 1 full block(s) were computed (num_computed_tokens=6, prompt=16)
```

With the fix both cases pass; the file's other <N> tests still pass (CPU only, macOS, no GPU run). Model outputs are unaffected, so no evals.

## Details

`_build_store_jobs` (`offloading/scheduler.py:1874-1883`) clamps the storable token count to `num_computed_tokens` only for `FINISHED_ABORTED`; every other finish uses `max(num_prompt_tokens, num_tokens - 1)`, which is the whole prompt for a request that produced no output. `storable_chunks` then only bounds by allocated blocks, so the half-written block goes out under its full hash. A request can finish this way mid-prefill through `finish_requests(..., FINISHED_ERROR)` (`sched/scheduler.py:2525-2540`): an encoder-cache mismatch, or a failed KV load under the `fail` policy.

Fix: `min(req.num_computed_tokens, max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1))`. The spec-decode clamp is kept.

Not a duplicate: #63010 (store cursor reset on a restart from token 0) and #60810 (the block table of a resumed streaming session), both merged on 10-25, and the open #62795 (flush promotions before a request's tiers are finalized) are adjacent; none touches this clamp.

AI assistance: I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to trace this path and write the test; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests myself.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Prefill locally while a peer handshake is pending
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A symmetric-P2P consumer now prefills locally instead of waiting while a session's handshake is pending, so a request that names a stopped or deleted source returns at once rather than after up to `VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S` (30 s). Closes the gap reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63602#issuecomment-6491634566.

## Claims

- `remote_kv_source` requests to a stopped (SIGSTOP), force-deleted or gracefully deleted source: p50 15.7–17.0 s / max 30.1 s → p50 22 ms / max 4.7 s. The worst case is now the 8 s lookup timeout, for a lookup already in flight when the source stops.
- No regression in the reproducer's other checks: A never freezes, A→C pulls stay at 100%, and pulls from B or its replacement B2 recover fully.
- The PD path (`remote_prefiller`) is unchanged and keeps its eager HIT.

## Validation

**E2E**, using the [reproducer from #63602](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63602#issuecomment-6491634566): three single-GPU Qwen3-0.6B engines on one 8×H200 node (mlx5 IB, NIXL), with a probe pulling a fresh ~2K-token prefix from B and C every 200 ms. The image is `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-3966924d` (it already contains #63207, #63779 and #64250) plus #64256 and #64251. **fix** adds this PR. The changed `vllm/` files were copied over the nightly at pod start. One run per case.

| case | build | requests to faulted B, p50 / max | > 15 s | B/B2 pulled after recovery | A→C pulled | PASS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1 SIGSTOP 60 s | base | 15.7 s / 30.1 s | 157/301 | 240/240 | 614/614 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.022 s / 4.7 s** | **0/304** | 239/239 | 615/615 | ✓ |
| c2 force-delete, B2 | base | 17.0 s / 30.1 s | 281/499 | 400/400 | 838/838 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.022 s / 0.038 s** | **0/502** | 400/400 | 842/842 | ✓ |
| c3 graceful delete, B2 | base | 17.0 s / 30.1 s | — | 400/400 | 841/841 | ✓ |
| | **fix** | **0.023 s / 0.036 s** | 0 | 400/400 | 837/837 | ✓ |
| c0 no fault | fix | — | — | 700/700 | 625/625 | ✓ |
| c7 SIGKILL, same IP | fix | 0.023 s / 0.078 s | 0 | 400/400 | 512/512 | ✓ |
| c8 rolling replace | fix | 0.053 s / 0.084 s | 0 | 400/400 | 589/589 | ✓ |

The c1 fix run's overall max (8.1 s) comes from the two probes sent ~1 s before the SIGSTOP. Their LookupMsg was already out, so they ended on the 8 s lookup timeout.

**Unit:**
- `test_lookup_before_handshake_ack_falls_back_to_local_prefill` fails without the fix (`RETRY != MISS`) and passes with it.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/`: 618 passed, 12 skipped.

## Details

**Root cause.** For a `remote_kv_source` request, `on_new_request` opens a session to the source, and `lookup()` registers a probe and returns RETRY until the LookupResp arrives. `ClientRole.flush_pending_lookups` holds probes until the peer acks ConnectMsg, and the 8 s lookup deadline only starts when the LookupMsg goes out. While the handshake is pending, the only bound on the request is the 30 s handshake deadline.

When the source stops or goes away:
1. The first lookup timeout ends the session.
2. No reconnect backoff applies, since backoff is scheduled only after a data-plane fault.
3. The next request opens a new session at once and waits on its handshake.

Each request therefore waits for whatever remains of the current 30 s handshake, which gives the ~17 s p50 and 30 s max.

**Fix.** `lookup()` treats a session that is not `ready` like a missing session and returns MISS. It returns before `register_lookup`, so the peer never gets lookup state for the request, and `finish` owes it no terminal FetchMsg. Inbound and outbound sessions both send ConnectMsg and become `ready` on the ack, so reused inbound sessions behave the same way.

**Tradeoff.** A request that arrives before its session's handshake completes now recomputes instead of pulling. That includes the first request to a new or replacement peer. Sessions persist across requests (idle ones are reaped only near `VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS`), so this costs one window per peer of about the handshake time, 14–40 ms of registration on these pods. The c8 rolling-replace run pulled 400/400 from B2. Recomputing a prefix is cheaper than waiting up to 30 s on a peer that may be gone.

**Not changed.**
- The reconnect backoff for timeout-ended sessions (the issue's other proposal) is not added. With this change, a dead peer costs at most one cheap connect attempt per handshake window, and no request waits on it.
- A lookup already in flight when its source stops still waits up to the 8 s lookup timeout (#63781).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Dedup transfer regions by (base_addr, block_len)
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #57661

- **Root cause**: NIXL region registration deduped transfer regions by `base_addr` alone, and the collapsed branch only refreshed block geometry for MLA regions. In hybrid-attention models, a layer with a different block length aliasing another layer's base address (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash compressor `state_cache` / indexer `k_cache` overlaid on `swa_cache`) was silently folded and inherited the first region's block length. PD transfers of its state were truncated and misaligned, producing garbled output with no errors.
- **Fix**: dedup key is now `(base_addr, block_len)`. Identical-geometry aliases still fold (`test_overlaid_transfer_groups_share_region_geometry` continues to pass, confirming the lossless path is unchanged).
- **Behavior change (maintainer sanity-check welcome)**: `test_ring_scratch_without_mamba_registers_and_addresses_its_own_regions` now expects `_scratch_region_indices == [2]` instead of `[1]`. That fixture (introduced in #56214) overlays rings on a paged region whose block_len differs from the rings' page size — the old expectation had recorded the benign form of this very bug (the ring inheriting the paged region's geometry). If overlay folding was intentional design, this one assertion is trivially revertible.
- **Tests**: added `test_shared_base_regions_with_distinct_block_lens_stay_separate` (two geometries at one base address — 256B MLA swa page vs 128B compressor ring page — must register as two regions with their own block lens and descriptor geometry). Verified in a container: target test fails on HEAD / passes with the fix; `test_nixl_connector_hma/push_connector/tp_mapping` failure sets are identical before/after. `ruff check` + `ruff format` pass.

**Why this is not a duplicate**: searched open issues/PRs (nixl region dedup, deepseek pd disagg, base_addr, garbled output); #52627 is Mooncake-specific and #54926 is un-transferred draft KV — different root causes.

**Model evals**: 2×8 H200 cluster, NIXL P/D disagg — before: fully garbled output; after: clean English/Chinese generations, 0% garble rate, 6 concurrent streams clean (details in #57661).

**AI assistance disclosure**: root-cause analysis and this fix were produced with ZCode (local agent); cluster diagnosis, the initial mitigation patch, and remote test runs were done with Chaterm (remote agent). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and performed the end-to-end cluster verification above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DBO] Create hipBLASLt handles in microbatch threads before graph capture
commits.pr_body:
Fixes a crash on ROCm during FULL CUDA graph capture with V2-runner DBO. It turned AMD CI's `test_dbo_v2_features_gsm8k` red after #61464: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98127#01a184f5-5c73-4e2a-9dc4-578724d0239d

- `ubatch_utils.py`: before capture, each microbatch thread runs a 1x1 GEMM on its compute and comm streams, so its hipBLASLt handles exist before capture starts.
- With this fix, V2-runner DBO with DeepEP low-latency starts on ROCm, both with and without spec decode. Before it, the server crashed in `hipblasLtCreate` (`hipblaslt.cpp:164`) every time.

On ROCm, PyTorch keeps one hipBLASLt handle per thread and stream and creates it lazily on the first GEMM. Creating one calls `hipMalloc`, which is not allowed while a stream is capturing. `CUDAGraph::capture_begin` creates the handle ahead of time, but only for the thread that starts the capture. With the V2 model runner, DBO runs the GEMMs on separate microbatch threads, and captures on a dedicated stream. When capture starts, the capturing thread takes a handle that a warmup microbatch thread had just released to PyTorch's handle pool. One microbatch thread then has to create a new handle mid-capture, and hipBLASLt exits the process. I confirmed this order of events by tracing every `hipblasLtCreate` and `getCurrentCUDABlasLtHandle` call by thread.

The pre-capture warmup added in #51700 only called `torch.cuda.current_blas_handle()`. On CUDA that object also serves cuBLASLt; on ROCm the hipBLASLt handle is a separate object. The bug has been there since #51700 (the commit before it rejects V2 DBO with CUDA graphs). It surfaced when #61464 added the first AMD CI test that runs V2-runner DBO.

The extra GEMM only runs on the capture path, once per microbatch thread per stream, before capture begins. Steady-state steps are unaffected. On CUDA it is a no-op apart from one tiny kernel before each DBO capture. The V1 runner's DBO capture has the same incomplete warmup but doesn't crash today, because its capture stream is one the main thread already holds a handle for; this PR leaves V1 alone.

Validated on MI350X (gfx950), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, DeepEP at the `Dockerfile.rocm` pin.

| Run | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py -k v2_features` | crash | 10/10 passed (`spec_decode`; `dcp` skipped, needs 4 GPUs) |
| `vllm serve` V2 DBO + `deepep_low_latency`, no spec decode | crashed 3/3 | — |
| Standalone torch repro (one worker thread doing the GEMMs during capture) | crashed 3/3 | passed 3/3 |

The existing `test_dbo_v2_features_gsm8k` covers this path in AMD CI, so this PR adds no new test.

commits.pr_title: [Mistral] Use get_grammar_for_chat_request in MistralParser and require mistral-common 1.13.0
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Switch `MistralParser.adjust_request` to mistral-common's single-pass grammar entry point `GrammarFactory.get_grammar_for_chat_request` (new in mistral-common 1.13.0) and require `mistral_common >= 1.13.0`.

## Claims

- vLLM no longer picks the grammar mode for Mistral tokenizers. It builds a mistral-common `ChatCompletionRequest` with `from_openai(**request.model_dump(include={messages, tools, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls}, exclude_none=True), response_format=...)` and mistral-common renders the grammar. This replaces the manual `get_lark_from_jinja` / `get_lark_for_json_schema` routing.
- `response_format` is passed to mistral-common unchanged and follows its defaults: a `json_schema` is enforced by the grammar only when `strict` is true; otherwise any JSON object or array is accepted. `structured_outputs.json` has no `strict` field and stays enforced. See the open question for maintainers on `_mistral_response_format`.
- `check_json_nesting` and the errors for unsupported `structured_outputs` / `response_format` types stay in vLLM.
- mistral-common validation errors (pydantic `ValidationError`, e.g. an invalid JSON schema, and `InvalidRequestException`, e.g. a JSON response format with tools and `tool_choice="required"`) surface as `VLLMValidationError` (400) instead of 500. See the open question for maintainers on the `except` line.
- Bump `mistral_common` to `>= 1.13.0` in `requirements/common.txt` and the test requirements; the compiled test pins move to `1.13.0`. Its dependency floors are already met by the existing pins, so no other pin changes.

### Behaviour changes for Mistral grammar-capable tokenizers

- **Text + no tools + `tool_choice` auto/None:** no grammar is attached and `_grammar_from_parser` stays `False` (previously a text grammar was attached).
- **`tool_choice="required"` or a named tool:** on the base template the model can no longer write text before the tool call; a named choice pins the tool name. Think templates are unchanged.
- **JSON response format + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`:** the grammar allows only the JSON answer or tool calls; plain text is rejected.
- **`json_schema` without `strict: true`:** the grammar constrains output to any JSON object or array instead of the schema (previously always enforced).
- **`json_schema` with no schema:** 400 (previously fell back to `json_object`).
- **`parallel_tool_calls: null`:** treated as allowed, as in OpenAI (previously `False`).

## Validation

macOS CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, mistral-common 1.13.0, xgrammar 0.2.8, huggingface_hub 1.31.0.

```bash
pytest tests/parser/mistral/ tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py tests/renderers/test_mistral.py \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_lark.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_replay.py tests/parser/engine/test_delegating_replay.py tests/parser/test_beam_parser.py
```

| Code | mistral-common | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | 1.13.0 | 5304 passed, 0 failed |
| `main` | 1.13.0 | 26 failed: `get_lark_from_jinja` now requires `force_tool_names`, and `reasoning_effort="medium"` is now accepted |

- New tests check the grammar text `adjust_request` returns for `required`, a named tool, and JSON schema + tools + `auto`. They fail when the grammar is changed back to allow free text before the tool call.
- New tests check that `strict` reaches mistral-common unchanged, that the schema appears in the grammar only when `strict` is true, and that an invalid schema raises `VLLMValidationError`.
- `pre-commit --hook-stage manual` passes, including the four `pip-compile` hooks. In the compiled test requirements only `mistral-common` moves to `1.13.0`, and `typing-extensions` drops it from its "via" list (mistral-common 1.13.0 no longer depends on it).
- Not run: GPU serving, end-to-end requests, model evals.

## Details

- `tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py`: existing `adjust_request` tests now patch `get_grammar_for_chat_request` and assert the request it receives. Added grammar-content, `strict`, invalid-schema and no-grammar tests. Removed the `null_tool_choice` case of the parametrized grammar test, since that request now correctly gets no grammar.
- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_lark.py`: pass `force_tool_names=False`, now required by `get_lark_from_jinja`. This is the only direct `get_lark_from_jinja` call left in vLLM.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py`: mistral-common 1.13.0 accepts all OpenAI `reasoning_effort` levels, so the test asserting `"medium"` is rejected is replaced by a check that every level is accepted.
- Removed the now-unused `_DEFAULT_JSON_SCHEMA` and the manual `tool_choice` / message / tool conversion.
- The non-grammar branch (pre-v11 tokenizers, unsupported structured outputs) is unchanged.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches `get_grammar_for_chat_request` or the mistral-common 1.13.0 bump.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Default Nemotron Omni mamba_ssm_cache_dtype to float32
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Maps the three Nemotron Omni architecture aliases to the existing `NemotronHNanoVLV2Config` in `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP`. With this mapping, the NemotronH Mamba SSM-cache default from #39032 (float32, or the checkpoint's own value) applies to them instead of silently falling back to bf16.

Related PRs:
- #39032: NemotronH float32 default and the `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2` hook.
- #52929: added the `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3` registry alias only.
- #55026: temporarily removed the Omni aliases.

No existing issue or open PR covers this. I searched open and closed vLLM issues and PRs for these architecture names, `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` with Omni, and `NemotronHNanoVLV2Config`.

## Claims

- **Default cache dtype:** for `NemotronH_Nano_Omni_Reasoning_V3`, `NemotronH_Super_Omni_Reasoning_V3` and `NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3`, `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=auto` now resolves through the NemotronH hook. That means float32, or the value in the checkpoint config, instead of the model dtype (bf16).
- **Nemotron 3 Nano Omni:** this fixes a large accuracy loss. GPQA Diamond goes from 51.9 to 68.4 with no flags, the share of generations that run to the token cap drops from 23% to 0.25%, and requests/s rises 2.55×.
- **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL:** the checkpoint's own `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype: float32` is now honored. Accuracy was within noise, but bf16 had a 4% runaway tail and about 30% lower throughput.
- **No change for explicit settings:** an explicit `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` still takes precedence, and other architectures are unaffected.

## Validation

**Regression test.** `tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py::test_omni_mamba_ssm_cache_dtype`, marked `core_model` so the "models/multimodal -m core_model" CI step selects it.
- It builds the real engine config via `EngineArgs(...).create_engine_config()` for the public Nano Omni and Super VL checkpoints. Only the config is downloaded, no weights.
- Cases: `auto` → float32, and explicit `bfloat16` is kept.
- Run in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.32.1rc1.dev197):

```
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_nano_nemotron_vl.py -m core_model
# without this PR
E  AssertionError: assert 'auto' == 'float32'
FAILED ...::test_omni_mamba_ssm_cache_dtype[auto-float32-nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16]
FAILED ...::test_omni_mamba_ssm_cache_dtype[auto-float32-nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16]
2 failed, 2 passed
# with this PR
4 passed
```

**End-to-end runs.** Setup: stock `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`, each model card's `vllm serve` command with no `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` flag. With this patch and no flag, the startup log shows "Updating mamba_ssm_cache_dtype to 'float32' for NemotronH model" and the SSM kernel config `cache_dtype=float32.json`. Without the patch, there is no update line and the kernel config is `float16.json`, which is how vLLM names bf16.

| Model (architecture) | SSM cache: before → after | GPQA Diamond: before → after | Gen. hitting token cap | Requests/s: before → after | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron 3 Nano Omni BF16 (`NemotronH_Nano_Omni_Reasoning_V3`), B200 | bf16 → float32 | **51.9 → 68.4** (float32 via flag: 70.1) | 23% → 0.25% | 0.147 → 0.375 (2.55×) | NVIDIA reported 72.2 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, RedHatAI FP8 (`NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3`), H200 x2 | bf16 → float32 | 88.6 → 89.1 (float32 via flag) | 4.0% → 0% | 0.175 → 0.249 (1.42×) | card 89.5 / 89.9 |
| `NemotronH_Super_Omni_Reasoning_V3` | not tested: no public checkpoint | — | — | — | — |

GPQA setup:
- NeMo-Skills `gpqa`, temperature 1.0, thinking on.
- Nano Omni: average of 4 runs, top_p 1.0, max 131072 tokens.
- Super VL: average of 2 runs, top_p 0.95, max 110592 tokens (card context 114688), with the RedHatAI card command minus its Mamba precision flags, as in the NVIDIA BF16 card.

Requests/s is completed requests ÷ benchmark wall time for the whole GPQA run, with the same client concurrency before and after. Nano Omni: 792 requests at max_num_seqs 384. Super VL: 396 requests at max_num_seqs 128. Repeated identical runs vary by about 2.5%.

With an explicit `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` and this patch, the cache stays bf16.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- `registry.py` maps the three Omni aliases to `("nano_nemotron_vl", "NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2")`.
- `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP` is looked up by the HF architecture string and only contains `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2`.
- So `NemotronHNanoVLV2Config.verify_and_update_config` never runs for the Omni aliases. `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` stays `auto`, which resolves to the model dtype.
- That hook is also the only place the checkpoint's `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` is read.
- The bug is present on v0.31.0, v0.32.0 and current nightly.

**Why float32.**
- Nano Omni: NVIDIA's report, [arXiv 2604.24954](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24954) §4.7, says "the Mamba SSM state cache is kept at FP32 at serving time". NeMo-Skills' Nemotron 3 Nano recipe, for the same LLM backbone, serves with `--mamba_ssm_cache_dtype float32`.
- Super VL: its checkpoint sets `llm_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype: float32` ([config.json](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16/blob/main/config.json)).
- #39032 made float32 the NemotronH default because "Only `float32` is known to have no accuracy issues by default".

**Why it matters.** bf16 rounding of the recurrent state shows up as runaway generations. Models served with MTP speculative decoding, such as Super VL here, are affected much less than Nano Omni.

**Tradeoff.** A float32 SSM state doubles SSM-cache memory and costs a few percent of decode throughput. On these models the net throughput still rises, because the runaway generations go away.

**Limitations.**
- `NemotronH_Super_Omni_Reasoning_V3` is included because it is registered to the same class. It has no public checkpoint to test.
- The mapping also applies `NemotronHNanoVLV2Config.verify_and_update_model_config`, which defaults the video backend to `nemotron_vl` via `setdefault`. Omni already uses the `NemotronH_Nano_VL_V2` model class, so this aligns it with that class.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, the patch, the test and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
