commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Fix Humming FP8 linear for per-tensor/per-channel FP8 weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60162. With the Humming FP8 linear kernel, `fp8` checkpoints with per-tensor weight scales and online `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel` quantization crash while loading weights. On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, Humming is the only FP8 linear kernel left (Marlin opts out of batch-invariant mode), so these models cannot start in that mode. Humming FP8 is W8A16, so `fp8_per_channel` (PTPC, which asks for per-token FP8 activations) now gets the same clear error as on Marlin instead of running.

## Claims

- `Fp8LinearMethod` (non-block) and `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` load and run on Humming. GSM8K accuracy is within about one standard error of Marlin.
- On Ampere with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, these models start and are batch-invariant under the default torch.compile + CUDA graphs.
- `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` rejects Humming with the same error it already raises for Marlin.

## Validation

Latest run, after merging main (Oct 26): one A40 (SM86) on Runpod, official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-00b6c4c565a8732c131e1f452d4a17803bb0842b`, with this PR's diff applied to the installed package. Raw logs: [PTPC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#discussion_r4383165873), [everything else](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#issuecomment-6428742135).

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_model_load_and_run` | `humming` case fails (stride error) | 3 passed, 3 skipped |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error)* | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.7544 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_tensor`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error)* | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.8673 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_channel`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error) | `ValueError`: Humming is W8A16 (same check as Marlin) |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_channel`, `--linear-backend humming` | — | same `ValueError` |

\* From the earlier runs below; main's code path for these is unchanged.

GSM8K is lm_eval `gsm8k` (5-shot, all 1319 questions), flexible-extract. For reference, on the Oct 20 RTX 3090 run, Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 in default mode (Marlin on both sides) scored 0.7642 on main and with this PR.

<details>
<summary>Earlier runs (Oct 6, Oct 15, Oct 20)</summary>

Rows that show `fp8_per_channel` starting on Humming predate the PTPC check.

**Oct 20**, RTX 3090, nightly `e68efc68`: repro, lm_eval and bench with raw logs in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60163#issuecomment-6286567601).

**Re-validated after merging main (Oct 15).** Head `671702b6e` (main `984c242ede` + this PR). Since main's latest wheel was not published yet, I used the precompiled extensions from `388a610dfb` (the only build change in between is the DeepGEMM tag) with torch 2.14.0, humming-kernels 0.1.17 and flashinfer 0.7.1, on an A40 inside the official nightly image's CUDA environment. Toggling between main and this PR was checked by SHA-256 of the touched files.

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (stride error) | starts; batch-invariant 3/3; GSM8K 0.780 |
| Qwen3-8B `fp8_per_tensor` / `fp8_per_channel`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | — | start; batch-invariant 3/3 each |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8, `--linear-backend humming` | — | GSM8K 0.784 (Marlin baseline on main: 0.772) |
| `test_model_load_and_run` with this PR's test | `humming` fails (stride error) | 3 passed |
| `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` | 3 `test_fp8_reloading` failures | same 3 failures, 26 passed |

GSM8K uses 500 questions, 5-shot.

The original validation below was done before the merge, on nightly `92044241`.

Run on the official image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691` on an A40 (SM86), with the container's environment. The installed source files were checked against commit `92044241` by SHA-256 before testing. "This PR" means this diff applied to the installed package; the touched files are unchanged between `92044241` and this PR's base. Batch invariance uses the reproducer from #59086: request A alone, alone again, then batched with a longer request B; 48 greedy tokens; 3 rounds.

| Model / quantization | Flags | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8` (`fp8`, per-tensor) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash: `self.stride(-1) must be 1 to view Float8_e4m3fn as Int ... but got 4096` | starts; A batched vs alone identical 3/3; GSM8K 0.790 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization fp8_per_channel` | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | crash (same error) | starts; identical 3/3 |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | starts; GSM8K 0.784 |
| Qwen3-8B `--quantization fp8_per_tensor` | `--linear-backend humming` | crash | — |
| Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8 (control) | default (Marlin) | GSM8K 0.786 | — |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8` (block, control) | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | works, identical 3/3 | — |

GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 500` (5-shot).

`test_model_load_and_run` now also runs with `linear_backend="humming"` (`pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_model_load_and_run -v`, same image):

| | auto | marlin | humming |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | passed | passed | **failed** (stride error above) |
| this PR | passed | passed | passed |

The rest of `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py` gives the same result with and without this PR on this GPU. Three `test_fp8_reloading` cases fail on the A40 either way with identical errors, and are unrelated to this change. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

</details>

## Details

**Missing layout tag.** `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy` returns the weight as a `(K, N)` transposed view, and `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` transposes it itself. Humming's `convert_linear_layer_to_humming_standard` reads `layer.processed_weight_dims` (falling back to the parameter's checkpoint `input_dim`/`output_dim`) to detect the layout. Without it, Humming assumes `(N, K)` and calls `.view(torch.int32)` on the transposed view, which fails. Since #62326, CompressedTensors, fbgemm, ModelOpt and Quark FP8 set `processed_weight_dims = (0, 1)` after transposing. This PR does the same in the two methods that lacked it. Humming is the only FP8 scaled-mm kernel that reads it, so other kernels are unaffected.

**PTPC.** `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` already refuses Marlin because PTPC requires per-token FP8 activations and Marlin FP8 is W8A16. `HummingFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` builds its layer without an input schema, so it is W8A16 too. With the layout fixed, PTPC would silently run as weight-only FP8 on Humming, so this PR adds Humming to that check. `Fp8LinearMethod` and `fp8_per_tensor` already accept Marlin's W8A16 fallback, and Humming matches it.

**Batch-invariant `apply`.** In batch-invariant mode these methods call the kernel only when `fp8_scaled_mm_is_batch_invariant()` (from #52231) says so; otherwise they dequantize `layer.weight` and run `F.linear`. After Humming's `process_weights_after_loading`, `layer.weight` is in Humming's packed layout, so that fallback fails (`a and b must have same reduction dim, but got [s, 4096] X [256, 24576]`). Humming has its own batch-invariant mode (`use_batch_invariant` in its compute config), and the block-FP8 path and compressed-tensors already call it in this mode. This PR makes `fp8_scaled_mm_is_batch_invariant()` return True for Humming. Humming FP8 is weight-only here, so the dynamic per-tensor activation amax that the helper guards against doesn't apply.

**Notes.**
- Without batch-invariant mode, two identical requests on Humming were not bitwise identical (first difference at token 4). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` they were. vLLM only promises this in batch-invariant mode, and it does not come from this change.
- CI: the new `humming` case is in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`, whose Quantization step is temporarily disabled by #63608. The layout bug does not depend on the GPU architecture. I validated on SM86 only.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open issues and PRs for Humming FP8 linear, the stride error message, the layout tags, and FP8 batch invariance on Ampere. #59460 also edits `scaled_mm/humming.py` (activation-quantization fallbacks) but not the weight layout or batch-invariant dispatch, and this PR does not touch `humming.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Update RADIO vision encoder to match the current Transformers version
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

vLLM's RADIO vision encoder (`radio.py`, added in #24595) is a fork of the original NVlabs remote-code RADIO: `ViTPatchGenerator` / `ClsToken` helper classes, a `model.`-nested module tree (`model.patch_generator.*`, `model.encoder.layers.*`), and a hand-rolled weight remapper that loads only the legacy remote-code checkpoint layout. This PR restructures it so the module tree and weight loading mirror the canonical Transformers `RadioModel` (`transformers.models.radio`), and fixes loading across the published C-RADIO checkpoint versions.

### Why v2, v3, and v4

vLLM's existing RADIO code (#24595) was written and tested against **C-RADIOv2** (`nvidia/C-RADIOv2-H`). The Transformers `RadioModel` this PR mirrors is shaped for **C-RADIOv4** -- its config defaults resolve to v4's token counts. Bridging the existing v2-era vLLM code to the v4-shaped Transformers modeling means the loader must span that range, so it supports **v2, v3, and v4** -- all published `C-RADIO*-H` checkpoints, which share one checkpoint layout and differ only in recipe counts (`teachers`, `register_multiple` / `cpe_num_registers`) that `RadioConfig` derives. `nvidia/C-RADIO` (v2.1 `mlpnorm`) is out of scope -- a different block architecture (per-block `mlp.norm`) that Transformers' `RadioModel` doesn't support either.

## Changes (relative to the existing vLLM RADIO)

- **Module tree** now mirrors the Transformers layout: the `model.`-nested `model.patch_generator.*` / `model.encoder.layers.N.*` becomes `embeddings.*` / `encoder.layer.N.*`. New `RadioPatchEmbeddings` / `RadioAttention` / `RadioLayer` (`norm1` / `attention` / `layer_scale1` / `norm2` / `mlp` / `layer_scale2`) / `RadioLayerScale` replace `RadioInternVisionModel`, the `ViTPatchGenerator` / `ClsToken` helpers, and the old `self.layers` / `attn` / `ls1` naming.
- **Weight loading**: the hand-rolled, legacy-only remapper is replaced by a `WeightsMapper` (`hf_to_vllm_mapper`) that maps the published checkpoint keys (`radio_model.model.blocks.*`, fused qkv) onto the new tree, and also accepts the native Transformers key layout. `load_weights` now warns when it matches zero tensors instead of silently leaving the tower at random init.
- **Config**: the token-count derivation (`num_cls_tokens` / `num_registers` / `summary_idxs`) moves from the model into `RadioConfig`. Adds `cpe_num_registers` -- C-RADIOv3 sets `register_multiple=0` and carries its register count there, and without deriving it the config built 4 register tokens where the checkpoint ships 8 (v3 failed to load). Adds `layerscale_value`.
- **Consumer**: `nano_nemotron_vl` vision-weight routing broadened (`vision_model.radio_model.` -> `vision_model.`) so RADIO tower keys reach `RadioModel`.
- **Tests**: `test_radio.py` previously covered only `C-RADIOv2-H`; now parametrized over `C-RADIOv2-H` / `v3-H` / `v4-H`, crops each image to the tower's own `min_resolution_step` (it differs across generations; the old crop hard-coded v2's geometry), and adds a weight-loading round-trip unit test.

### Unchanged from the existing vLLM RADIO (noted because they differ from Transformers)

- Attention keeps vLLM's **existing** fused `QKVParallelLinear` (renamed `attn.qkv` -> `attention.qkv`) rather than HF's split `query`/`key`/`value` -- required for tensor-parallel + quantization; the mapper fuses native split projections into it and loads the legacy fused tensor directly.
- Image normalization stays in the input processor (mean/std from config); `input_conditioner` weights are dropped, as before, avoiding fp16/bf16 precision loss.
- Dynamic-resolution packed attention (`MMEncoderAttention`), video temporal compression, and TP/quantization support are carried over unchanged.

### Why the derivation is needed

vLLM consumes NVIDIA's published `config.json` as-is, which states only the recipe (`teachers`, `register_multiple` / `cpe_num_registers`) -- never the resulting token counts, so `RadioConfig` derives them. (Transformers' `RadioConfig` instead states v4-shaped defaults and doesn't read these fields, and `AutoModel` refuses these repos entirely -- `auto_map` remote-code, no `model_type: radio` -- so it cannot load them without a caller supplying the counts from outside.)

## Testing

`pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_radio.py -v` -> **9 passed** (NVIDIA GB200, transformers 5.17.0). Cosine similarity is vLLM vs. the NVlabs remote-code reference (`trust_remote_code`):

| checkpoint | dtype | params loaded | cosine (summary / features) |
|---|---|---|---|
| nvidia/C-RADIOv2-H | half, bf16 | 387/387 | 1.000000 / 1.000000 |
| nvidia/C-RADIOv3-H | half, bf16 | 387/387 | 1.000000 / 1.000000 |
| nvidia/C-RADIOv4-H | half, bf16 | 387/387 | 1.000000 / 1.000000 |

The `RadioConfig`-derived token counts and `summary_idxs` also match each checkpoint's stored tensors exactly (v2/v3: 8 tokens, `[0,1,2]`; v4: 10 tokens, `[0,1]`).

## Model evaluation

Behavior-preserving for the models that use RADIO. Branch-vs-stock A/B on MMMU (`mmmu_val`) for two public checkpoints, verified from both arms' server logs (identical model, image, TP, decoding, and doc set):

| model | MMMU config | stock (upstream RADIO) | this branch | answer rate | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron-Nano-12B-VL | `--limit 20`, greedy | 0.5150 | 0.5150 | 95% | equivalent, no change |
| Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B | n=600, temp 0.6 / top-p 0.95, TP=4 | 0.6217 +/- 0.019 | 0.6667 +/- 0.018 | 76% | no detectable difference (~1.7 sigma), no regression |

The 30B gap is within this model's run-to-run spread at temp 0.6 (repeated measurements span ~0.045) -- not an improvement. Both 30B scores are floors: ~24% of responses never reach an answer letter and are random-guessed equally in both arms. Merging this PR does not regress either supported model.

## Not a duplicate

Updates the existing in-tree RADIO (added in #24595) to track current Transformers; not a new/competing implementation.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance. A human author reviewed every changed line, and the tests and evaluation above were executed on GPU with their outputs verified.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Bench] Aggregate DP running requests for profiling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix Rust bench's deferred profiling on data-parallel servers by summing `vllm:num_requests_running` across the engine series exposed by `/metrics`.

## Claims

- DP8 with 16 running requests per engine now reports 128 to `--profile-batch-threshold`, instead of 16. A threshold of 120 can therefore be reached.
- Match the exact gauge name and read its sample value before an optional timestamp. Preserve zero versus missing metrics and clarify the aggregate threshold in CLI help.

## Validation

Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.95.0. From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test --offline --locked -p vllm-bench
cargo clippy --offline --locked -p vllm-bench --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Raw test summaries (unit tests, then CLI parity tests):

```text
test result: ok. 190 passed; 0 failed; 12 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 2.60s
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
```

Four synchronous parser tests cover DP sum, exact-name matching, zero versus missing metrics, and timestamps. The original parser fails the DP sum, exact-name, and timestamp cases; all four pass after the fix. Clippy and pre-commit pass.

## Details

The previous parser returned the first matching series. vLLM exports this gauge per engine, so the profiling threshold could remain unreachable despite sufficient total concurrency. Aggregate valid samples while excluding metric names that merely share the prefix. Client-side metric parsing and help text only; no new dependencies.

The total matches the aggregate scope of `--max-concurrency`, rather than requiring a minimum batch size on each engine. With uneven DP load, profiling may start while some engines still have small batches. Only engines exposed by the target `/metrics` endpoint are counted.

Duplicate check: no matching open PR found for `fetch_num_requests_running`, `profile_batch_threshold`, or Rust DP profiling.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Support thinking_token_budget in the Responses API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63663. `/v1/responses` now accepts `thinking_token_budget` and passes it to `SamplingParams`, as `/v1/chat/completions` already does.

## Claims

- `thinking_token_budget` on `/v1/responses` now limits reasoning. Before, it was silently dropped, because `ResponsesRequest` did not declare it and `OpenAIBaseModel` allows extra fields.
- Validation is shared with Chat Completions through the `ThinkingTokenBudget` type: `-1` means unlimited, and other negative values return 400 instead of being ignored.
- The field shows up in the rendered Responses extra-params list (via the `responses-extra-params` snippet), and the "Thinking Budget Control" docs now mention it.

## Validation

**Server regression test** (`RemoteOpenAIServer`, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, reasoning parser `qwen3`): the new `test_thinking_token_budget_responses_api` sends the same greedy request with `thinking_token_budget=5` to both endpoints and checks that the reasoning text matches.

```bash
pytest -v tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_thinking_token_budget.py
```

- Base commit (85e199e60): fails, because Responses ignores the budget.
  ```
  E   assert '\nOkay, the ...r should be 2' == '\nOkay, the user'
  E     - Okay, the user
  E     + Okay, the user is asking "What is 1+1?" and wants a concise answer. Let me think. ...
  FAILED ...::test_thinking_token_budget_responses_api[default]
  ```
- With this PR: `7 passed, 1 skipped` for the whole file (the skipped test needs 2 GPUs for FP8 + MTP). I also ran the new test 3 more times, and it passed each time.

**Unit test**:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_sampling_params.py
```

10 passed. Without the fix, `test_extra_sampling_params` fails with `assert None == 128`.

**Manual E2E**: 1x H20 running `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3 --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str": "<think>", "reasoning_end_str": "I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now.</think>"}'`. Each request is greedy with `max_output_tokens=2048` and the prompt "9.11 and 9.8, which is greater? Think carefully." Reasoning tokens are counted with the model tokenizer, because Responses `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` is not populated for `SimpleContext`.

| Request | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/responses`, no budget | 200, 535 reasoning tokens | 200, 535 |
| `/v1/responses`, `thinking_token_budget=16` | 200, **535** (ignored) | 200, **29** (same text as chat) |
| `/v1/responses`, `thinking_token_budget=-1` | 200, 535 | 200, 535 (unlimited) |
| `/v1/responses`, `thinking_token_budget=-2` | **200** (ignored) | **400** `` `thinking_token_budget` must be a non-negative integer or -1 for unlimited. `` |
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `thinking_token_budget=16` (reference) | 200, 29 | 200, 29 |

(29 = 16 budgeted tokens + the forced `reasoning_end_str` phrase.)

## Details

- Root cause: `ResponsesRequest` never declared `thinking_token_budget`, so the request body accepted it as an extra field and `to_sampling_params()` never forwarded it.
- Fix: declare the field with the shared `ThinkingTokenBudget` annotated type and forward it in `to_sampling_params()`, the same way as `ChatCompletionRequest`. There are no serving-layer changes; the budget is enforced by the existing sampler path.
- The server test lives in the existing `chat_completion/test_thinking_token_budget.py` so it can reuse that module's Qwen3-0.6B reasoning server instead of starting another one in the Responses CI step.
- Not a duplicate: there is no open PR for #63663. #43692 tried the same change earlier and was closed without review.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Rust vllm-bench accepts --max-concurrency 0 and hangs forever (Python rejects it since #54887)
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #64319.

Rust `vllm-bench` accepted `--max-concurrency 0` and then hung forever on `Semaphore::new(0)`, while Python `vllm bench serve` rejects 0 since #54887. This change rejects 0 fail-fast on every Rust bench path that builds a concurrency semaphore:

- Serve path (`config.rs`): `--max-concurrency 0` and `--multi-turn-concurrency 0` are rejected with a clear error instead of hanging.
- Sweep path (`sweep.rs`): any 0 in `--sweep-max-concurrency` is rejected before the first sweep point runs.
- `mm-processor` path (`mm_processor.rs`): `--max-concurrency 0` is rejected at the entry point, before the managed engine is spawned, since this subcommand does not go through `BenchConfig::from_args`.

Why this is not duplicating an existing PR: a search for open PRs mentioning #64319 returns only this PR, and #64319 itself has no linked PR.

Tests run:
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`: 191 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.
- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib concurrency`: 8 passed, 0 failed (the zero/positive max-concurrency, multi-turn, and sweep cases).

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reduce CPU overhead for warm FlyDSL launches by reusing compiled host launchers instead of repeating JIT argument binding and cache-key construction. Covers DeepSeek V4/V4.1 mono decode, Kimi K3 specialized decode, TurboQuant and UltraQuant.

## Claims

- Fix all nine remaining in-tree FlyDSL host launchers using the warm JIT path.
- Reduce measured host enqueue overhead by approximately 88% for TurboQuant and 89% for UltraQuant.

## Validation

Measured on gfx950 with PyTorch 2.10.0 and FlyDSL 0.4.0: 30 alternating batches of 100 launches, with GPU synchronization outside timed sections. Times are median (min–max), µs.

| Launcher configuration | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TurboQuant: B1, Hk8, GQA8, D128, BS16, context256 | 72.33 (70.71–74.15) | 8.57 (8.15–9.74) |
| UltraQuant: B1, Hk1, GQA8, D256, BS32, context2048 | 73.57 (72.98–79.64) | 8.30 (8.08–10.94) |

Existing GPU correctness suites: **68 passed before and after**. Dynamic batches **1→2→4→8→3→1** reuse the same compiled callable and match reference outputs. Dynamic arguments, row strides, compile-only and graph replay checks passed; pre-commit including mypy passed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/kernels/turboquant/test_flydsl_turboquant_decode.py \
  tests/kernels/ultraquant/test_flydsl_decode_d256.py
```

Validation used a source-only editable installation. Full-model accuracy, TP serving and end-to-end performance were not measured because the target checkpoints and a complete ROCm extension build are unavailable.

## Details

Targets host dispatch during warm eager execution and graph capture. The results measure host enqueue time; steady graph-replay speedup was not measured. Open-PR searches found no duplicate fix for these call sites.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Consume prompt embedding sentinel IDs before model execution
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix chat requests that mix prompt embeddings and images when the prompt-embedding placeholder ID is outside the model vocabulary. Consume these temporary IDs during preprocessing instead of passing them to token validation and embedding lookup.

Discovered while helping validate vllm-project/vllm#58658 and vllm-project/vllm#63190, but this is a distinct issue: the fix consumes temporary placeholder IDs in the renderer, rather than changing tower/connector LoRA or prompt-embedding passthrough handling in the runner.

## Claims

- Replace only prompt-embedding placeholder spans with safe dummy token IDs after locating all spans.
- Preserve surrounding text IDs, supplied embedding tensors, and embedding offsets.
- Fix the request rejection and avoid the TP=1 out-of-bounds embedding lookup, without tokenizer-cache, model-runner, or model-specific changes.

## Validation

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/test_hf.py::test_apply_prompt_embeds_keeps_engine_token_ids_in_vocabulary -q

PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion_with_prompt_embeds.py::test_prompt_embeds_with_image -v
```

| Validation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Renderer regression | Fails the vocabulary-bound assertion without the two-line fix | Passes; all IDs are in vocabulary, text IDs are unchanged, and both embedding spans retain their offsets |
| SmolVLM-256M serving, TP=1 | Mixed image/embedding request returns HTTP 400 | Generates one token successfully; invalid ordinary completion token IDs still return HTTP 400 |
| Gemma 4, TP=1 and TP>2 | Original HTTP 400 reproduced on this model | Submitter confirmed the local reproducer succeeds at TP=1 and TP>2 |
| Nemotron 3 Nano Omni | Original request returns HTTP 400 | Submitter confirmed the local reproducer succeeds |

The serving regression was also run with only the two-line normalization change present, with no tokenizer-cache changes: **1 passed**. The relocated renderer regression passed: **1 passed**. All commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, and test-tethering checks.

Model validation is limited to the generation smoke test and the submitter's Gemma and Nemotron reproducers; no accuracy or performance benchmark was run.

The original failure was reproduced locally with:

- `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16`
- `Google/gemma-4-E2B-it`
- `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct`

The original failure was not observable with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B`, `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-450M`, or `llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf`. Qwen3.5 and LFM2.5 have model-vocabulary headroom for the newly registered sentinel, so the stale cached vocabulary bound does not reject it. These are locally checked examples, not an exhaustive affected-model list.

Thanks to @gatedd and @ajf-codes for helping me identify the issue!

<details>
<summary>Manual reproducer: mixed prompt embeddings and image input</summary>

Start a server with `--enable-prompt-embeds`, using the same model as `MODEL_NAME` below. TP=1 also exposes the unsafe embedding lookup if the validation rejection is bypassed without consuming the sentinel.

```bash
vllm serve Google/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --enable-prompt-embeds \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1
```

Save the following script locally and run it with `.venv/bin/python mre.py`. It downloads the tokenizer and the checkpoint shard containing the token embedding weights, constructs real prompt embeddings, and sends them alongside an image. The image URL requires network access. Set `MODEL_NAME` to another listed model and restart the server to compare models.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Send multimodal + prompt embeds to a local vLLM server and print the response."""

import json
import pprint

import httpx
import torch
import transformers
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from huggingface_hub.errors import RemoteEntryNotFoundError
from safetensors import safe_open

from vllm.utils.serial_utils import tensor2base64

# MODEL_NAME = "nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16"
MODEL_NAME = "Google/gemma-4-E2B-it"
# MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"
# MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B"
# MODEL_NAME = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2"
# MODEL_NAME = "LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-450M"
# MODEL_NAME = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct"
# MODEL_NAME = "llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf"
SERVER_URL = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions"


key_name_lookup = {
    "nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16": "language_model.backbone.embeddings.weight",
    "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B": "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B": "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2": "model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "Google/gemma-4-E2B-it": "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-450M": "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct": "model.text_model.embed_tokens.weight",
    "llava-hf/llava-onevision-qwen2-0.5b-ov-hf": "language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight",
}


def load_embedding_layer(
    model_name: str,
    key: str | None = None,
) -> torch.nn.Embedding:
    if key is None:
        key = key_name_lookup[model_name]

    try:
        index_path = hf_hub_download(model_name, "model.safetensors.index.json")
    except RemoteEntryNotFoundError:
        shard_name = "model.safetensors"
    else:
        with open(index_path) as f:
            index = json.load(f)
        shard_name = index["weight_map"][key]

    shard = hf_hub_download(model_name, shard_name)
    with safe_open(shard, framework="pt") as f:
        weight = f.get_tensor(key)
    return torch.nn.Embedding.from_pretrained(weight)


def encode(
    tokenizer: transformers.PreTrainedTokenizerBase, embedding_layer, text: str
) -> str:
    token_ids = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False).input_ids
    prompt_embeds = embedding_layer(token_ids).squeeze(0)
    return tensor2base64(prompt_embeds)


def main() -> None:
    tokenizer = transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_NAME, trust_remote_code=True
    )
    embedding_layer = load_embedding_layer(MODEL_NAME)

    messages = [
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "This part is text. The part that follows will be prompt embeddings. Please tell me the color they say.",
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "prompt_embeds",
                    "data": encode(
                        tokenizer,
                        embedding_layer,
                        "This part is prompt embeddings. The color is purple. End prompt embeds.",
                    ),
                },
            ],
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {
                        "url": "https://fastly.picsum.photos/id/373/200/300.jpg?hmac=GXSHLvl-WsHouC5yVXzXVLNnpn21lCdp5rjUE_wyK-8"
                    },
                },
            ],
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Please describe the image to me. Then tell me my favorite color.",
        },
    ]

    request = {
        "model": MODEL_NAME,
        "max_tokens": 1024,
        "temperature": 0.0,
        "messages": messages,
    }

    r = httpx.post(SERVER_URL, json=request, timeout=600)

    print("-" * 30)
    if r.status_code == 200:
        response_json = r.json()
        print("-" * 30)
        pprint.pprint(response_json)
        print("-" * 30)
        print(response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])
    else:
        print(r.status_code, r.text)
    print("-" * 30)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

The mixed-input path already records the positions and tensors needed for embedding splicing, but leaves the temporary sentinel IDs in `prompt_token_ids`. A newly registered sentinel can exceed the cached tokenizer's vocabulary bound, causing HTTP 400. If validation accepts the sentinel, an out-of-range model embedding lookup can instead crash before the supplied embedding is merged. TP>1 shard masking can hide that latter failure.

After locating all spans, replace their token IDs with `0` and write the updated list back to the engine input. The existing multimodal merge overwrites those dummy embeddings with the supplied tensors. Ordinary token IDs are not changed, so their validation remains intact.

The production change is two added lines. Tests cover two embedding spans of different lengths and real TP=1 image/embedding serving; documentation describes mixed image and prompt-embedding inputs.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching open upstream PR. The related vllm-project/vllm#51123 addresses LoRA batch-shape handling in the runner, not mixed-input sentinel consumption in the renderer.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector] Support sleep mode with MooncakeStoreConnector
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #59625 (merged). Rebased onto main.

MooncakeStoreConnector registers the GPU KV cache with the Mooncake store (`register_buffer`). Over RDMA, that registration pins the physical pages. Sleep mode unmaps the KV cache, and wake maps new pages at the same virtual addresses. The store keeps using the old pages, so puts and gets read and write memory the model no longer uses.

Evidence on main (GB300, Qwen3-8B, two instances sharing one store; instance A sleeps at level 1, instance B never sleeps):

- After the wake, every store hit on A gives wrong output: 0/8 for KV that B put, and 0/8 for A's own post-wake puts.
- A's puts after the wake store stale bytes. B reads them and also returns wrong output (0/8), even though B never slept.
- While asleep, A still holds 67.8 GB of GPU memory, because the KV cache stays pinned. After the wake it holds 150.8 GB (85.4 GB before the sleep).
- There are no errors and no log lines.

On main, this combination is refused at startup ("MooncakeStoreConnector does not support sleep mode").

This PR implements the sleep-mode hooks from #59625 for MooncakeStoreConnector:

- `unregister_kv_caches()` runs before the KV cache is unmapped. It waits until the put queue and the shared get queue have no queued or running tasks, then calls `unregister_buffer` on each device KV region. All store puts and gets run on those queues; lookups only query keys.
  - The wait is bounded by `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` (480 s by default), the same bound `MooncakeConnector.unregister_kv_caches` uses. That is well above Mooncake's 60 s per-transfer timeout, so a slow queue does not fail the sleep. On timeout it raises `TimeoutError` and keeps the registration. The wait shares one helper with `close()`.
- `restore_kv_caches()` runs after the KV cache is mapped again. It registers the same addresses and lengths.
- Both calls are all or nothing and idempotent. If an (un)register call fails partway, the calls already made are undone and the error is raised. A failed sleep leaves the engine awake and fully registered; a failed wake leaves the regions released, so a retry starts clean.
- Host-resident (HiSparse) regions are host memory, which sleep does not touch, so they stay registered.
- `supports_sleep_mode()` reads the protocol from the Mooncake config file (`MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`). The workers use the same file to set up the store. It accepts `rdma` and `tcp` and refuses other configured protocols. The check runs only when sleep mode is enabled, and it does not import mooncake. If the config is missing, startup fails with the existing "MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH is not set" error.
  - Why RDMA and TCP: no peer holds a key to our KV cache. Puts and gets use our local lkey against peers' host-DRAM segments, so registering again locally is enough.
  - TCP registration only records the address range. Data moves with `cudaMemcpy` on the virtual address, and nothing is pinned.
  - Other configured protocols (e.g. nvlink) can export handles to peers, so they stay refused.
  - It also refuses when `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` or `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` is set. Mooncake then installs an nvlink transport even with `protocol: rdma`. Like Mooncake, it checks only that the variable is set, not its value.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests (CPU, fake store), one per invariant:
  - Release and restore round-trip exactly the device regions, with the same addresses and lengths (dense layout, and HiSparse with one host group plus one device group). Both calls are idempotent across two cycles.
  - Release waits for a queued or running put or get. A real thread finishes the task when a `threading.Event` is set. A timeout keeps the registration.
  - A failed unregister or register is rolled back, and a retry then succeeds.
  - The config gate: rdma/tcp accepted; nvlink, `MC_FORCE_MNNVL` (also `=0`) and `MC_INTRANODE_NVLINK` refused; missing config. Mooncake is blocked from import.
- Mutation check: each piece of the change was altered on its own (gate and each env var, region recording, host skip, idempotence, state, lengths, rollback, each drained queue, the bound, the deadline). 23 mutants, all killed, and every test kills at least one.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/{test_config,test_mooncake_store_*,test_mooncake_connector,test_multi_connector}.py tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py`. The store tests were also run 5 times. pre-commit was run on the changed files.
- Hardware (GB300, Mooncake 0.3.13.post1, RDMA, standalone `mooncake_master`, Qwen3-8B):
  - Two servers share one store: A sleeps and B never sleeps. GPU prefix caching is off, so every cached token comes from the store.
  - 8 random 2048-token prompts per phase, greedy decoding, 32 output tokens.
  - After every cycle: A gets KV that B put, B gets KV that A put after the wake, and A gets its own post-wake put back.
  - Cycles: 3× `/sleep?level=1` + `/wake_up`; 1× level-1 sleep then `/wake_up?tags=weights` and `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`; 1× `/pause` + `/release_kv_cache_memory` + `/wake_up?tags=kv_cache`.
  - Control run: `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points. This performs the same store wipe as sleep, without unmapping anything.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (`test_config`, `test_mooncake_store_worker`, `test_mooncake_connector`, `test_multi_connector`, `test_sleep_mode_backend`): 407 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `test_multi_connector.py` and are unrelated to this change: one needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, the other needs `ray`, which is not installed. They fail the same way on #59625 alone. All `test_mooncake_store_*` files: 332 passed in each of the 5 runs.
- Hardware, sleep run vs awake control: 224/224 outputs are token-for-token identical across all 28 phases. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store.
  - Before this change, each post-wake hit phase was 0/8.
  - Each run also compares hits with the cold output of the same prompt. A few phases there show 7/8, and the control run shows exactly the same mismatches. These come from near-tie prompts where a store hit and a cold prefill differ, not from sleep.

| GPU memory on A | this PR | main (earlier run) |
|---|---|---|
| awake | 85.1 GB | 85.4 GB |
| asleep, level 1 (3 cycles) | 2.1 GB each time | 67.8 GB |
| after wake | 85.1 GB each time | 150.8 GB |
| selective wake: weights only | 19.4 GB | — |
| after `release_kv_cache_memory` | 19.7 GB | — |

- After the review changes (rollback, env check, shared drain), a shorter rerun on the final commit with 2 level-1 cycles gave 104/104 outputs identical to its control. Every hit read 2032 tokens from the store. A held 2.1 GB asleep and 85.1 GB awake in both cycles.
- Transfer errors: none in either run (non-zero error counters, glog `E` lines, `ERROR` lines, and tracebacks were all 0 on A and B).

Not covered:

- TCP on hardware. On this cluster, TCP puts and gets fail with `TRANSFER_FAIL` even without sleep, with both P2PHANDSHAKE and the HTTP metadata server. An earlier H200 run of main with TCP and sleep returned 8/8 with memory fully freed, but it was not repeated with this commit.
- The HiSparse path on hardware (unit-tested only).
- TP > 1 and multi-GPU runs.
- The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`). The drain inside `unregister_kv_caches` is what covers it there.

Known limitations:

- Mooncake builds with NVLink support (such as the cuda13 wheel) also install an nvlink transport when they find no RDMA NIC. That can't be detected at config time, so it is not refused.
- Pre-existing: sleep at level ≥ 1 and `release_kv_cache_memory` reset the connector before the release. On rank 0 that reset waits for the put queue with no bound, so a stuck put hangs there, not in the bounded release.
- Pre-existing: a load task that raises before the `try` in `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread._handle_request` never calls `task_done`. The drain then never sees an empty queue, and every later sleep fails with `TimeoutError`. We found no scheduler input that reaches it. A fix needs a load-error report too, so it is left for a follow-up.
- Pre-existing, not specific to this connector: `/sleep?mode=wait` (and `/pause?mode=wait`) while connector loads are in flight returns 500 "Failed to reset KV cache ...", and the scheduler stays paused until `/resume`. Under `PAUSED_NEW` the scheduler counts only running requests, so requests holding blocks for an async load look idle. Use `mode=abort`, or call `/resume` and retry.

Known separate issue, not fixed here: sleep at level ≥ 1 resets the connector, which runs `remove_all(force=True)` on the Mooncake master. One instance's sleep therefore deletes the KV of every instance that shares the master. It should be scoped by tenant.

### Additional Test Result: stress run

- Stress run (GB300, 1 node, Qwen3-8B, Mooncake RDMA, one shared store; the image plus per-file mounts of this stack, sha-checked):
  - Three servers: TP2 and TP1 sleep with staggered, overlapping windows, and a TP1 server never sleeps; `store_tp_size=2`, so TP2 and TP1 share keys. 20 cycles. After each wake: get of keys another server put while it was asleep, own put read back, and cross-server read-back of its post-wake puts.
    - 2080/2080 outputs are token-identical to an awake control run (`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` at the same points). Every hit read 2032/2048 tokens from the store.
  - TP2 plus a never-sleep server, 10 cycles: full sleep, selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`), and `release_kv_cache_memory`. 400/400 identical to control.
  - Memory had no drift: TP2 at 3583 MiB/GPU asleep and 86467 woken, TP1 at 2077 / 85101, the same in every cycle. Host RSS of each server was unchanged from cycle 1 to cycle 20. 0 transfer errors.
  - 64 concurrent requests up to `/sleep?mode=wait`, with puts in flight: 64/64 complete, 0 timeouts, and requests not yet scheduled run after the wake. `mode=abort`: all aborted, and sleep takes 0.5 s.
  - HiSparse (GLM-5.2-FP8 TP4, HiSparse + MooncakeStore through MultiConnector): 78 host regions stay registered and the device region is released and registered again. 12 `release_kv_cache_memory` cycles: device memory returns to the same value every cycle, and store hits read 4160+ tokens. Exact-retrieval accuracy on store hits after a release equals an interleaved control on the same prompts (72/96 vs 72/96, with 140/144 per-request outcomes equal). Level-1 sleep was not run on this model: it would back up about 704 GB of weights to host RAM.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Fix MiniMax-M3 docstring cross-references
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Format tensor shapes and array indexing as inline code in three MiniMax-M3 AMD docstrings, fixing the seven unresolved cross-references that abort strict API documentation builds.

Fixes #64469. The [failing Read the Docs build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35491049/) contains the original warnings.

## Claims

- Render the shapes and indexing literally, avoiding unintended `head`, `:n`, and `r` cross-references.
- Keep the change to three docstrings; the AST is identical after removing docstrings.

## Validation

Python 3.12.13 with the repository-pinned `requirements/docs.txt`:

```bash
READTHEDOCS_CANONICAL_URL=https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/ \
  .venv/bin/python -m mkdocs build --clean \
  --site-dir /tmp/vllm-docs --config-file mkdocs.yaml --strict
```

- Base `fa3b9d1377219247060d3c8b49eae199c9e7e154`: exit 1, reproducing all seven warnings (`head` ×2, `:n` ×4, `r` ×1); output: `Aborted with 7 warnings in strict mode!`.
- Patched tree, same command and dependencies: exit 0, zero MkDocs/autorefs warnings; output: `Documentation built in 112.08 seconds`.

commits.pr_title: [Performance][KV Offload] Avoid zero-filling the SimpleCPUOffload host KV pool
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Large `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` host KV pools are zero-filled during startup even though CPU blocks become loadable only after a completed GPU-to-CPU store. The target configuration allocates about **175 GB per rank**; use `torch.empty` to avoid a redundant full-buffer write at that scale.

## Claims

- Removes eager zero-filling of the CPU KV pool while preserving tensor shapes, dtypes, capacity, and host registration.
- No end-to-end startup speedup is claimed; GPU pinning and serving validation are pending.

## Validation

Validation ran with this patch applied to upstream main `0fddee1f5869465a6235d2076f82f1ea70318064`. GitHub's subsequent merge preview contains identical offload runtime and test code; the intervening main changes add unrelated model recipes.

- `VLLM_PLUGINS='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -q --maxfail=1`: **100 passed, 1 skipped**. The CUDA/ROCm worker module skipped on this macOS host; the passing scheduler tests cover CPU store/load bookkeeping, not GPU DMA.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py`: all applicable hooks passed, including Ruff 0.14.0 and mypy. `git diff --check` passed.
- Allocation-only microbenchmark: Apple M4, macOS arm64, PyTorch 2.11.0, one CPU thread, 256 MiB `int8` tensor, seven alternating-order samples after two warmup iterations:

| Allocation | Median | Min–max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch.zeros` | 3.616 ms | 3.592–3.618 ms |
| `torch.empty` | 0.750 µs | 0.625–2.500 µs |

This measures an unpinned allocation with a warm allocator. It excludes page population during registration, CUDA/ROCm registration, GPU store/load traffic, and model startup. It must not be extrapolated to a serving speedup. Required performance follow-up: compare allocation plus host registration at **175 GB per rank**, including the actual concurrent ranks per host, and measure end-to-end startup/output behavior. The existing Buildkite `v1-kv-offload` step covers the worker suite on CUDA and its ROCm mirror; those runs and the production-sized comparison remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Allocation-only reproducer</summary>

Run in a PyTorch 2.11.0 environment:

```sh
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import statistics
import time
import torch

torch.set_num_threads(1)
samples = {"zeros": [], "empty": []}
for iteration in range(9):
    modes = ("zeros", "empty") if iteration % 2 == 0 else ("empty", "zeros")
    for mode in modes:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        if mode == "zeros":
            tensor = torch.zeros(256 * 1024**2, dtype=torch.int8, device="cpu")
        else:
            tensor = torch.empty(256 * 1024**2, dtype=torch.int8, device="cpu")
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        del tensor
        if iteration >= 2:
            samples[mode].append(elapsed)
for mode, values in samples.items():
    print(mode, "median/min/max seconds:", statistics.median(values), min(values), max(values))
PY
```

</details>

## Details

`vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` contains the only logic change and a brief safety comment. The manager inserts CPU block hashes in `_process_store_completion` after all workers report the store complete; CPU lookups and loads use that cache. Unwritten CPU blocks are therefore unavailable for loads. `cudaHostRegister` still runs and retains its page-faulting and pinning cost.

Duplicate-work check: #60130 replaces the per-layer allocations with a shared host mapping and optional HugeTLB pages; #54578 and #54792 add asynchronous initialization, and #54792 still allocates zeroed buffers. This PR is the minimal allocation-only change to the current synchronous path, without a buffer-layout or readiness redesign.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Refresh CPU LRU for GPU-hit prefixes in eager SimpleCPUOffload
commits.pr_body:
Ready for review.

## Overview

With eager `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, a prefix that keeps hitting the GPU prefix cache is the first thing evicted from the CPU cache, because its CPU copy never leaves its first-store LRU position. When a request with a GPU prefix hit is admitted, this PR moves the CPU copy of that prefix to the MRU end.

## Claims

- Eager mode keeps hot GPU-hit prefixes on CPU; lazy mode is unchanged.
- Kimi-K3 agentic disaggregated benchmark on MI355X at `be4275d22`: +8.7% total tok/s/GPU, mean TTFT 8.6 s to 5.3 s.

## Validation

- New `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_lru` (full attention) and `test_gpu_prefix_hit_refreshes_cpu_mamba_boundary` (attention + Mamba) fail on main and pass here. The second also catches refreshing only full attention, freeing in forward order, or refreshing at lookup.
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/` and the SimpleCPUOffload connector, metrics and NIXL unit tests at `be4275d22`: 179 passed, 8 skipped (optional integration tests). pre-commit clean.
- End to end: one run per configuration, below.

<details><summary>End-to-end benchmark</summary>

Kimi-K3, agentic multi-turn trace at concurrency 48, 1 prefill + 1 decode instance on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8, FP8 KV cache, `MultiConnector` of MoRIIO and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (`lazy_offload: false`, 1.8 TB) on the prefill instance. vLLM ROCm nightly `81198e97`; "after" mounts this PR's `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` at `be4275d22`, ported onto the nightly; server config otherwise identical. Both ran on 2026-10-26 with prefill on the same node; decode nodes differ.

| | [before](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40286897952/job/121452690051) | [after](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/40300366703/job/121496601447) |
|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s/GPU | 9783 | 10638 (+8.7%) |
| TTFT mean / p90 | 8.58 s / 21.71 s | 5.27 s / 11.08 s |
| TPOT p90 | 20.50 ms | 20.08 ms |
| Prefill tokens recomputed per request | 6160 | 5178 (-15.9%) |
| Prompt tokens loaded from CPU | 5.0% | 5.4% |

The first revision (`edf0671ce`, refresh at lookup) measured [9658](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38850989926) to [10616](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/39054120919) tok/s/GPU in the same setup.

</details>

## Details

Root cause on the prefill instance:

1. Turn 1 computes prefix X; the eager store copies X to CPU.
2. Later turns hit X on GPU. Eager stores skip blocks already on CPU, so X's CPU copy is never touched.
3. Other requests' stores evict CPU blocks in LRU order, so X goes first although it is the hottest prefix.
4. When GPU pressure later evicts X, the next turn misses both tiers and recomputes X.

In eager mode, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` records the GPU hit length and `update_state_after_alloc` refreshes that prefix once at admission, so a request waiting for blocks does not repeat the CPU lookup each step. The refresh runs `cpu_coordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` over the prefix, then touches and frees the result in reverse order like `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.free`: every full-attention block, the sliding window and the Mamba state at the boundary.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCM][Bug] Elastic DP doesn't work with AITER-on
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Elastic EP Scaling test (distributed/test_elastic_ep.py::test_elastic_ep_scaling) failed with AITER on. The cause is:
1. AITER requires a torch.distributed-registered group, but Elastic EP is using stateless group, which is not torch.distributed registered at all, so we need to skip AITER AR and choose next available AR;
2. During scale-up, existing workers call _release_cuda_graphs() and then re-capture into the same global graph pool. Some memory in that pool was still allocated, because FlyDSL didn't release them correctly. Graph replay never re-enters Python, so a kernel last launched during capture holds those tensors inside the graph pool indefinitely. The pool had no graphs left but still had live blocks, so PyTorch rejected capturing into it again. Now I explicitly call _switch_to_fresh_graph_pool() to switch to a new graph pool to avoid this.

## Claims

These 2 bugs are fixed. This test case works as expected no matter AITER is on or off.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][AMD] A GPU-CPU KV transfer fault in OffloadingConnector takes the engine down instead of degrading the cache.
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

A GPU<->CPU KV transfer fault in `OffloadingConnector` takes the engine down, although the connector
declares itself a best-effort cache (`requires_kv_delivery` is False, `offloading_connector.py:74`:
*"a dropped save is just a future cache miss"*).

On main (f47792af7f):
- `swap_blocks_batch` raises through `STD_TORCH_CHECK` when the batch copy fails
  (`csrc/cache_kernels.cu:229` on ROCm, `:187` on CUDA). A device error latched by earlier work on
  the transfer stream surfaces at `end_event.query()`.
- No caller catches it. The V1 mixin starts async loads and submits deferred stores inside a bare
  `try/finally` (`kv_connector_model_runner_mixin.py:86-90`); the V2 `pre_forward` / `post_forward`
  (`v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py:70`, `:131`) and `gpu_model_runner.handle_preemptions` have no
  handler at all.
- The failure channel is dead code: `offloading/worker.py:286-288` asserts `transfer_result.success`,
  and its only producer hardcodes `success=True` (`cpu/gpu_worker.py:715`).

## What this changes

Faults are reported, not raised.

- **Submit fault** (`transfer_async`). The `RuntimeError` is caught, and the error the failed copy
  left pending on the thread is cleared. On ROCm the batch call does not read it, so without the
  clear the next kernel launch raised `hipErrorInvalidValue` and killed the engine anyway (measured
  on MI355X). `end_event` is still recorded on the failing stream and the job is queued as a failed
  transfer, so `wait()` and the next job's stream ordering still fence it. It is reported as failed
  only once that event completes, because copies enqueued before the failing one may still be
  running. Its stream, events and descriptor buffers are not returned to the pools.
- **Poll / wait faults.** `get_finished` reports a `RuntimeError` from `end_event.query()` as
  `TransferResult(success=False)`; `wait()` no longer raises and leaves reporting to the next poll.
  Only `RuntimeError` is downgraded (device faults raise it); anything else still propagates.
- **Failed store.** The worker marks the job failed in `OffloadingWorkerMetadata.failed_jobs` (kept
  across ranks by `aggregate`), and the scheduler calls `complete_store(success=False)`, so the
  chunks are never published as cache, and drops the KV event metadata recorded for them. Serving
  is unaffected: the chunk is simply not cached.
- **Failed load.** Its destination blocks hold undefined KV, so the request is reported through
  `KVConnectorTransferResults.failed_recving`, which the scheduler handles for any number of KV
  cache groups (block-level reports are rejected for more than one group since #56855). The outcome
  follows `kv_load_failure_policy`:
  - `fail` (the default): the request finishes with an error; other requests keep being served.
  - `recompute`: the request is rerun from scratch. It is marked `load_failed`, so its later lookups
    skip the offloaded cache and a persistent fault cannot reload the same chunks forever. Other
    requests still read those chunks, since the CPU copy itself is intact.

Scope: this covers the batch-copy path (ROCm 7.1+, CUDA 12.8+ drivers). The per-copy fallback in
`csrc/cache_kernels.cu:237-247` ignores `cudaMemcpyAsync` return codes and behaves as on main.

## Not a duplicate

- #50984 (merged) and #56855 did this for Mooncake; this PR follows the same `failed_recving` design
  for `OffloadingConnector`.
- #56032 (open) handles disk I/O failures in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`; no file overlap.
- #42461 (open, dormant) would remove the per-block API; this PR no longer uses it.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/kv_offload/
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py   # real weights
```

Plus an engine-level fault injection (a real `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` failure from a zero-size
descriptor) with `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, for store and load faults, both policies, with
and without a concurrent request.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-fe4df3df` (torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, HIP 7.15), sources
overlaid:

| suite | main f47792af7f | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/` + `tests/v1/kv_offload/` | 2713 passed, 12 failed | 2737 passed, 12 failed |
| `test_offloading_connector.py` (real weights) | 4 passed | 4 passed |

The 12 failures are identical on both sides and environmental (no `ray`, offline HF hub, Mooncake
bootstrap DNS); the +24 are this PR's tests. Each of the 7 fixes was reverted individually and turns
its test red.

Engine-level fault injection (real weights, `kv_load_failure_policy` as noted):

| fault | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| store | engine dies | chunk dropped; later output identical to the no-fault run |
| load, `fail` | engine dies | that request ends with `finish_reason=error`; a concurrent request and later requests are unaffected |
| load, `recompute` | engine dies | request recomputed; output identical, no reload |

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write and test this change; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Fuse tiny-M MXFP8 quant into the block32 GEMM; guard lm_head skinny-GEMM by weight size
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Two decode-time fastpaths for DeepSeek-V4.x block32 MXFP8 linears on MI355X (gfx950): fuse the tiny-M activation quant into the block32 GEMM (one launch instead of two), and guard the lm_head skinny-GEMM dispatch by weight size (weights far larger than L2 stay on the generic GEMM fall-through).

Part of the DSV4.1-Flash MI355X serving fastpath series — four **independent** PRs on `main`@90c4a1a73e, each reviewable and mergeable separately, in any order. Siblings: #63180 (fused shared experts), #63181 (fused draft sampling), #63182 (draft-prepare fastpaths). The four series PRs all register kill switches in `vllm/envs.py` at the same anchor and therefore conflict textually with each other there; the resolution is to keep both sides. This branch trial-merges cleanly into current `main`.

## Claims

- **Fused quant+GEMM** (`rocm_block32_gemm.py`): at M ≤ 8 (decode shapes) the block32 linear path launched `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` solely to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads. The fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the same arithmetic — one launch instead of two, no activation round trip. Bit-exact against the stock two-launch path at all eligible shapes (tuned tiers, masked K tail, in-launch split-K); ineligible inputs (non-contiguous x, fp32 x, M > 8) fall back bit-identically. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM`.
- **lm_head skinny-GEMM guard** (`layers/utils.py`): `wvSplitK_hf_sml` re-reads the weight matrix once per K-shard, so its effective bandwidth collapses on weights far larger than L2 — at TP=4 the DSpark draft vocab-parallel lm_head shard ([32320, 5120] bf16, ~315 MiB, one call per decode step) hit this collapse. Weights above `VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES` (default 256 MiB) stay on the generic hipBLASLt fall-through at 1 < n ≤ 5; n = 1 (no pathology) is unchanged. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD`.
- **−117 µs median decode ITL (−2.1%) on the current base** (`main`@`717cf84342`) — official DSV4.1-Flash serving command at TP=4 on MI355X, every paired run faster (rebase re-check under Validation). The submission-base study measured **−2.45% (−177/−188 µs)** over 12 position-balanced A/B cycles, and the win holds at the same magnitude across bases and images (−127 µs on the nightly ROCm-10 re-verification, −117 µs on the rebased tip). TTFT unchanged within noise.

## Validation

**Benchmark** — official serving command (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=5, `--monokernel`, MI355X), measured at TP=4; both fastpaths key on batch/weight shapes, not TP size. Both arms run this branch's tip; the OFF arm disables only this PR's two levers. 12 position-balanced A/B cycles (blocked AAA BBB, then BAB, then ABA), fresh server per arm per cycle, 2 sampled + 1 greedy client run per cycle (16 prompts, ISL 16 / OSL 2048, concurrency 1); arm statistic = median of per-run mean ITL; every lever's engagement asserted from the server log before the client runs.

| metric | ON median | OFF median | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ITL t>0 | 7.065 ms | 7.243 ms | −177 µs (−2.45%) |
| ITL t0 | 6.977 ms | 7.165 ms | −188 µs |
| TTFT t>0 | 24.70 ms | 25.01 ms | −0.31 ms |
| TTFT t0 | 24.74 ms | 25.68 ms | −0.94 ms |

11 of 12 sampled cycles faster (one boundary overlap: ON max 7.148 ms vs OFF min 7.120 ms).

**Nightly ROCm-10 re-verification** — re-measured on the current nightly ROCm-10 image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly, TP=4, same command and protocol; one fresh boot per arm, 2 sampled + 1 greedy run each): ON 5.498 ms vs OFF 5.625 ms median mean-ITL → **−127 µs (−2.27%)**, fully disjoint per-run ranges (ON 5.438–5.510, OFF 5.550–5.636), spec-decode acceptance parity (sampled-run means 3.29 vs 3.34).

**Rebase re-check** — rebased onto the latest `main`; the runtime diff is unchanged, with one added test-only commit hardening the skinny-GEMM guard tests against dropped ROCTracer captures (the profiler flake behind the `amd-mi300-model-executor` CI failure). Full local CI-equivalent suites on this tip: model_executor 1313 passed, benchmarks 219 passed. Same A/B protocol: ON 5.510 ms vs OFF 5.627 ms median mean-ITL → **−117 µs (−2.09%)**; every paired run is faster (sampled −133/−92 µs, greedy −169 µs), and both arms' censuses assert the fused path engaged / disabled respectively.

**Accuracy** — gsm8k, 5-shot, strict match, 1319 samples, one run per arm: ON 0.9325, OFF 0.9242. Both inside the 0.9196–0.9340 band observed across repeated draws of this build; across the series the paired on/off deltas scatter on both sides of zero (engine run-to-run scatter) and no arm falls outside the band.

**Tests** — the fused-quant tests live in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` next to the other `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` tests (the standalone file from the first revision is gone). Beyond the bit-exactness-vs-stock comparison, the serving-shape test now also checks the fused output against a high-precision QDQ reference — dequantize both MXFP8 operands and contract in fp32, independent of the block32 GEMM kernel under test (rel err < 5e-3) — so a regression in the GEMM itself cannot hide behind the bit-exact comparison. All tests pass locally on MI355X (gfx950):

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py \
       tests/model_executor/layers/test_lmhead_skinny_gemm_guard.py -q
111 passed, 15 warnings in 47.26s
```

Of the 111, the tests added by this PR are 28 items — 21 fused-quant tests (~1.8 s) and 7 skinny-GEMM-guard tests (~1.4 s); the rest of the wall time is interpreter/import startup and the pre-existing MXFP8 suite. Single MI355X GPU, nightly ROCm-10 image.

CI notes: the fused-quant tests are CDNA4-gated (`current_platform.is_rocm() and supports_mx()`) and skip on MI300 CI pools — they are validated locally above; the skinny-GEMM guard test runs on any ROCm GPU (needs the `wvSplitK` custom op). The full pre-commit suite passes on the changed files (ruff, typos, mypy, check-torch-cuda-call, check-test-tethering, check-forbidden-imports, ...), and every commit is DCO-signed.

The tip adds review-driven changes over the benchmarked tree — tests centralized into the existing file, the QDQ reference, the kill switches renamed to `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_*`, and the long docstrings trimmed to the dispatch rules (benchmark details now in this description) — plus two earlier lint-level fixes (`torch.accelerator.synchronize()` for pre-commit `check-torch-cuda-call`, a local `args: tuple` annotation in `rocm_block32_gemm.py` for mypy). No serving-path semantics change: the renamed kill switches are the only env-facing difference.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

Server (ON arm) — official serving command, as measured at TP=4 (the fastpaths are not TP=4-specific):

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --port 8123 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --block-size 128 --monokernel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

OFF arm: identical, plus `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM=1 VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD=1`.

Load (after a 4-prompt warmup; add `--temperature 0` for the greedy run):

```
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --port 8123 --backend openai --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 2048 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 90,95,99 \
  --save-result
```

Accuracy (same engine config; `max_model_len 16384` and no `cpu_offload` are the only harness deviations):

```
python -c '
import lm_eval
lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
    model="vllm",
    model_args=dict(
        pretrained="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
        max_model_len=16384, tensor_parallel_size=4,
        tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41", gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        block_size=128, moe_backend="aiter", monokernel=True,
        attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4",
                          "indexer_sparse_logits": True},
        compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8]},
        speculative_config={"method": "dspark",
                            "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
                            "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
                            "rejection_sample_method": "block",
                            "enable_adaptive_verification": False}),
    tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5, batch_size=8)'
```

</details>

## Details

**Fused quant+GEMM.** At M ≤ 8 the block32 linear path pays a full `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` launch just to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads; the fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the exact same arithmetic. Eligibility is a shape-table hit (serving shapes at TP=4 covering the K-structure variety: multi-band K=5120 with the in-launch split-K tier, the masked-K-tail K=1280, a small-K tile, and the default-config tier); degenerate activation blocks (all-zero, denormal, huge, negative-mirror) quantize identically, and CUDA-graph capture/replay is bit-exact in both counter states. The per-row-scale dispatch branch of the linear kernel is unaffected.

**lm_head skinny-GEMM guard.** The guard is a byte-size predicate on the weight at the skinny dispatch site: above the cap, at 1 < n ≤ 5, the call goes to the generic hipBLASLt GEMM (the same kernel class the n=6 path uses); below the cap, or at n=1, or with the kill switch, dispatch is stock. The swap is not bit-exact (different GEMM kernel, different accumulation order) — numerics are checked within bf16 GEMM tolerance, and the decision table, dispatch selection, env behavior and one-shot-per-site census warning are pinned by tests.

Both paths log their engagement as WARNINGs (one line per site/state), so ON/OFF arms can be asserted from the server log before benchmarking.

<details><summary>MI355X measurements behind the skinny-GEMM guard</summary>

Measured on MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=4, vocab-parallel `[32320, K]` bf16 lm_head shards, from serving traces and isolated microbenches:

- The DSpark draft lm_head `[32320, 5120]` (315.5 MiB, n=5, once per decode step) ran `wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 5>` at **1.55 TB/s** (213.8 µs/call in-graph), while the generic fall-through class runs the same GEMM at **~6.5 TB/s** (~51–73 µs).
- The n=6 target-verify lm_head `[32320, 7168]` (442 MiB) already dispatches to hipBLASLt `Cijk MT64x16x512` (56.2 µs/call in-graph, 7.9 TB/s), i.e. the fall-through kernel is fast and CUDA-graph-capture-safe in this exact serving configuration.
- Isolated microbench on the target-shape shard at n=5: wvSplitK 313.3 µs vs `torch.linear` 71.2 µs (4.4×).
- The n=1 variant (`wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 1>`) shows no pathology on large weights (6.9 TB/s on the 442 MiB shard); its fall-through (LLMM1) would be a numerics change with no speed win, so n=1 keeps stock dispatch.

The mechanism is weight re-reads: `wvSplitK_hf_sml` streams the weight once per K-shard, so above L2-sized weights the effective bandwidth collapses. This is orthogonal to VGPR-spill fixes in the skinny kernel itself (#63015, #62846) — see the related-PRs note below.

</details>

**Related PRs.**

- #63015 / #62846 (skinny-GEMM tile/spill fixes): the guard here addresses a different mechanism — weight re-reads vs L2 bandwidth on very large weights — not VGPR spills, so the two are orthogonal and compose. The spill fixes should recover `wvSplitK` throughput on shapes that spill; the re-read cost on weights far above L2 remains. Once either lands we can re-measure the `[32320, 5120]` n=5 shard on top of it and revisit the guard's byte cap / n-window if the fixed `wvSplitK` wins there.
- #59782 (fused MXFP8 quant, draft): same fused-quant idea, per-shape cutoffs and keeps the fusion past M=8 on some shapes, where this PR caps every shape at M=8 with a bit-exactness contract against the stock path. In our measurements the fusion works well at M ≤ 8; we have not measured beyond that and are happy to coordinate on which approach to keep.

---

commits.pr_title: [New Model] Add MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Model and Kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The first PR of the split of #63232. It adds the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash model code (everything under `vllm/models/minimax_m3`, NVIDIA and ROCm, including the DSpark draft) and all kernel changes. The model-runner, sampling and KV cache manager changes from #63232 are left out and will follow as separate PRs (plan under Details).

## Claims

- **Serve MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on Blackwell (SM100/SM103/SM107):** the NVFP4 routed experts of the MXFP8 checkpoint load through the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE with per-token FC1 input scales. The KV cache and the index-K cache run in NVFP4 on the MSA CUTLASS Q8KV4 kernels.
- **DSpark speculative decoding:** a draft model that defaults to the checkpoint's `dspark/` subfolder, with fused draft kernels and a `FLASHINFER_TS` backend for non-causal draft blocks.
- **Decode kernels:**
  - fused QKV+indexer MXFP8 GEMM epilogue;
  - SM100 fused dense GEMM1;
  - persistent QK-norm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel;
  - small-batch MoE finalize fused into all-reduce + Gemma norm + MXFP8 quant;
  - DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (opt-in, with expert parallelism);
  - opt-in NVFP4 indexer decode context parallelism at TP4.
- **ROCm:**
  - NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer on gfx950;
  - one-launch-per-layer FlyDSL mono decode;
  - small-M MXFP8 linear tuning;
  - gfx942 fallbacks.

## Validation

Unit tests ran on GB300 (SM103) against this branch, with MSA `25c1447` (the pinned version) vendored and CUDA 13.4 for the Q8KV4 JIT:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/attention -k minimax_m3` | 219 passed, 64 skipped (ROCm/other-SM) |
| fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV insert, DSpark draft kernels, MegaMoE, `tests/models/minimax_m3`, Qwen3-DFlash MXFP8 context KV, reasoning parser, speculative config, `FLASHINFER_TS`, DFlash/DSpark spec-decode unit tests, aux hidden states over PP, M3 multimodal processing, `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | 689 passed, 5 skipped, 3 failed (below) |
| `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (2 GPUs) | 57 passed, 5 skipped |

The 3 failures (`test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`) fail identically on `main` in the same environment. They are not caused by this PR.

**End-to-end on this branch.** `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` served with the command below (TP4 on GB300, NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer, DSpark k=7). Higher is better. MAL is the mean number of tokens accepted per verify step, out of 8.

| Eval | Config | Score | DSpark MAL |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k (1319) | chat path, 5-shot, `thinking_mode: disabled`, T=0, max_tokens 2048 | 0.9287 flexible / 0.9196 strict | 4.77 |
| aime26 mean@16 (30 × 16) | chat path, `thinking_mode: enabled`, T=1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 98304 | 0.9271 (pass@16 0.9667) | 3.48 |

Neither run had request errors. gsm8k had no truncated or unanswered rows. On aime26, 11 of 480 samples (2.3%) hit the max_tokens limit, and they are the only unanswered rows.

**On #63232 (the full branch)**, same setup with thinking on (aime26 mean@16, MMMU-Pro strict-match over 3460 questions):

| Arm | aime26 | MMMU-Pro strict | DSpark MAL (aime26 / MMMU-Pro) |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 0.9458 | 0.7936 | – |
| DSpark k=7 | 0.9208 | 0.7861 | 3.33 / 3.21 |

The two arms ran on different revisions of #63232. The paired comparison on one revision was within noise: aime26 +0.00 pp (95% CI ±3.0 pp), MMMU-Pro McNemar p=0.876.

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -tp 4 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "FLASHINFER_TS", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
```

Not covered:
- ROCm was not run (no AMD hardware here); the ROCm code is from the AMD contributors' branch and tests.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was not run.

## Details

**Shared code this PR touches.** All of it is opt-in or a no-op for other models:
- `FusedMoEConfig.qat_activation_key` (default `None`): a model declares the activation scheme its experts were QAT'd against. `make_nvfp4_moe_kernel` now raises instead of silently dropping `per_token_activation` for a backend that cannot honor it.
- `ModelOptMxFp8Config.moe_quant_algo` (default `None`): routes `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4` experts to the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE.
- `Attention(query_pre_quantized=False)`: lets the DSpark draft skip a second query quantization.
- `DraftModelSpeculator.attn_vllm_config`: the draft's metadata builders now see the draft overrides (attention backend, KV cache dtype). The copies are shallow, so engine-resolved state such as `cache_config.kv_cache_layout` survives. Covered by `test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.
- New `FLASHINFER_TS` attention backend, `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp`, a MiniMax-M3 TP check for NVFP4 KV, and the MSA pin bump (`968061a` → `25c1447`).
- The CuTe DSL primitives of the DeepSeek-V4.1 all-reduce and the Kimi-K3 latent MoE tail move to `vllm/models/common/ops/moe_tail_fusion`, shared with the M3 finalize fusion. Their callers only change import paths.

**For reviewers:**
- The ROCm mono decode here (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO`) predates and overlaps the upstream M3 MonoKernel (#62712, `kernel_config.monokernel`). The two need reconciling; it can also move to its own PR.
- `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp` (NVFP4 indexer, TP4) sits next to the existing `minimax_m3_indexer_cp` (ROCm bf16 Triton CP).
- The Q8KV4 prefill keeps a per-device split workspace that is only allocated on SM107. It was a stopgap on the source branch.

**Split of #63232.** Later PRs:

| PR | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| this | MiniMax-M3.1 model + DSpark draft + kernels | – |
| 2 | ROCm NVFP4 → MXFP8/MXFP4 online re-quantization and fused shared experts through the online quantization API (needed to serve the NVFP4-expert checkpoint on ROCm) | – |
| 3 | NIXL P/D for per-head-contiguous NVFP4 pages (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | this |
| 4 | FA4: no descale tensors for a unit per-tensor scale | – |
| 5 (deferred) | DSpark/DFlash sampling performance: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, batch-sharded draft sampling, wide DFlash padding, top-k/top-p | this |
| 6 (deferred) | KV cache manager: keep KV zeroing for mixed-precision groups | – |
| 7 (deferred) | SimpleCPUOffload HugeTLB host buffer (not MiniMax-specific) | – |

<details>
<summary>Where the excluded files of #63232 go</summary>

- **PR 2:** `quantization/online/*` (incl. `shared_expert.py`, `requantization.py`), `quantization/utils/config_utils.py`, `fused_moe/{utils,routed_experts}.py`, `quark/*`, `nvfp4_emulation_utils.py`, `base_config.py`, `model_loader/utils.py`, the NVFP4 oracle's re-quantization hook, the dequantize-iterator change in the ModelOpt/CT NVFP4 MoE, and the ROCm NVFP4-expert guard and FSE resolver in `minimax_m3/amd/model.py`.
