commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Fail a timed-out load at once, defer releasing its slots
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Part of #63602 (gap 2, consumer half). A timed-out P2P load now fails at the load timeout. Its destination chunks stay held until the peer confirms its WRITEs ended (AbortAck/TransferDone), or until the session ends.

This is the P2P side of the deferred-release API from **#63779** (merged). It replaces the consumer slot quarantine proposed in #61667 and supersedes #63715, whose disconnect-on-missed-AbortAck is folded in.

Three commits on main: #63715's disconnect on a missed AbortAck (`ac5c9806e6`) with its test constant fix (`0262efcc3a`), then the deferred release (`f00e9c6710`).

## Claims

- **The request falls back 5 s sooner.** A load that times out is reported failed at once, instead of after a further `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S`: 10 s instead of 15 s for symmetric P2P, 30 s instead of 35 s for PD. The same applies to `finish()` of an in-flight load.
- **No early slot reuse.** The failed load's chunks stay out of the free pool until AbortAck, a late TransferDone, or session close. Before, the abort-ack timeout and `close()` freed them through `complete_write(False)` while the peer's WRITE might still land in them.
- **Every hold is bounded.** A missed AbortAck disconnects the peer (the folded-in #63715), and `close()` sets every held load's release.

## Validation

New and updated tests, run with this PR's test files on the code before the deferred-release commit (#63779 + main + #63715). 8 fail for the reported reason:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py \
    -k "TestClientFlows or holds_chunks_until_abort_ack or carries_its_deferred_release"
E  ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)          # no failure at the load timeout
E  AttributeError: 'LoadResult' object has no attribute 'deferred_release'
E  AssertionError: assert 7 not in {7: JobMetadata(...)}                # job still pending at the load timeout
E  TypeError: LoadResult.__new__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'deferred_release'
8 failed, 8 passed
```

`test_timed_out_load_holds_chunks_until_abort_ack` drives a real `TieringOffloadingManager` and `CPUPrimaryTierOffloadingManager`, with a real `P2PSession` as the P2P tier. At the load timeout the job finishes, the key misses, and the chunk is held (`num_deferred_release_chunks == 1`, the free count unchanged). After AbortAck, the chunk returns to the free pool.

With this PR:

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.../nvidia/cu13/lib pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py
408 passed
$ pre-commit run --files <changed>      # mypy included
Passed
```

The #63602 consumer scenario, with a WRITE that never ends:
- the load fails at 30.001 s, with its release unset;
- the abort-ack timeout disconnects the session;
- `close()` sets the release.

All of this is CPU-only, and CI runs it in `misc.yaml`. GPU e2e is pending. The plan is to drop inbound `abort_fetch` on the source pod and check three things: fallback at about 10/30 s, `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_deferred_release_chunks` rising and then returning to 0, and the hold histogram at about 5 s.

## Details

**Root cause.** `JobResult` used to carry both the outcome and the memory release, so P2P had to pick one of two problems:
- Report late: on a load timeout, keep the job until AbortAck or `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S`.
- Free too early: an abort-ack timeout, or `close()` on peer death, reported `success=False`. The TieringManager then freed the chunks through `complete_write(False)` with the peer's WRITE possibly still landing.

#63779 splits the two. This PR uses it.

**Lifecycle of a load in `ClientRole`:**

| event | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| load timeout / `finish()` | send AbortFetch, keep job | send AbortFetch, **report failed now** with `deferred_release=Event()`, keep load |
| AbortAck | report failed | `event.set()`, no second result |
| late TransferDone | report its result | `event.set()`, no second result (request already fell back) |
| AbortAck timeout | report failed (chunks freed) | no result; record `expired_abort_ack`, which makes the session disconnect |
| `close()` | fail every in-flight load (chunks freed) | set every held load's event; in-flight loads not yet reported fail as before |

**The release point is ack or disconnect**, as agreed in #61667 ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#issuecomment-6418290229)). Two cases remain:
- **A WRITE that is stalled but still alive when the session ends.** On the source side this is covered by #64250, which keeps unconfirmed WRITEs across teardown, and #64251, which faults a peer whose WRITE stalls. Whether NIXL teardown fences a stalled WRITE stays open on #63602.
- **Loads never sent** (still queued before ConnectAck) also fail through `close()`, without a deferred release. Nothing was posted for them.

**`drain_jobs()`** keeps polling while any held load remains. Each hold is bounded by the abort-ack timeout and then the disconnect, which meets #63779's rule that every event is set before `drain_jobs()` returns.

**Why not #61667 as is:** it re-reports the same `job_id` with `memory_safe=True`, which needs parallel quarantine tables. It also rejects `reset_cache()` with `UnsafeTransferError` and a retry loop. #63779's alternatives section covers this. Here each job has exactly one outcome, and the release carries none.

Complexity: about 110 non-test lines in `p2p/` (client 154+/−, manager +10), plus #63715's 44.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] DSA: all-reduce partial hidden_states before PP send
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes wrong activations at every pipeline-parallel stage boundary for DSA models (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/{nvidia,amd}/model.py`, which serves DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x) when TP > 1. The last layer's un-reduced MLP/MoE output is now all-reduced into the residual before the PP send.

Separate from, and complementary to, #59961 (stage-local shared indexer top-k).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 BF16 with TP8PP2 now matches TP16 on GSM8K accuracy and on output length. Without this fix, it loses 7–9 points and generates about 7.6× more tokens.
- No extra all-reduce: it moves from the receiving stage to the sending stage, and `residual` is no longer sent. There is no change when PP = 1.

## Validation

All runs use GLM-5.3 BF16 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`) on 2 nodes × 8 B200 with the default 39/39 layer split. Every TP8PP2 row also includes the #59961 top-k fix, so this PR's effect is isolated. The TP8PP2 runs used vLLM 0.30.0 with an earlier, numerically equivalent variant of this fix (`residual += all_reduce(hidden_states)`, then send zeros as `hidden_states`). The changed model files are unchanged between 0.30.0 and current `main`, apart from this diff.

**GSM8K.** `lm_eval` 0.4.13 against `vllm serve`, first 100 test examples, zero-shot, greedy, `max_gen_toks=16384`. The prompt and filters are from `gsm8k_cot_llama`, with no stop strings so the reasoning isn't cut off. Generated-token counts come from the server's `/metrics`.

| Layout | strict-match | flexible-extract | Mean generated tokens | Hit 16k cap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP16 (reference) | 0.94 ± 0.024 | 0.94 ± 0.024 | 224 | 0 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 | 0.87 ± 0.034 | 0.85 ± 0.036 | 1,707 | 7 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 + **this PR** | **0.95 ± 0.022** | **0.95 ± 0.022** | **225** | **0** |

With the fix, total generated tokens are 22,461, against 22,446 for TP16.

**Long-form sampling.** `LLM.generate` on 128 reasoning prompts, temperature 1.0, fixed seeds, `max_tokens=8192`.

| Layout | Capped at 8192 | Mean output tokens | >10% repeated 16-grams | Multiple `</think>` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP16 (reference) | 37% | 4,638 | 3 | 0 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 | 78% | 7,055 | 17 | 6 |
| TP8PP2 + #59961 + **this PR** | 41% | 4,687 | 3 | 0 |

<details>
<summary>GSM8K reproduction</summary>

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray --reasoning-parser glm47 --served-model-name glm

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=glm,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=100,tokenized_requests=False \
  --apply_chat_template --include_path <dir with gsm8k_glm.yaml> --tasks gsm8k_glm --limit 100
```

`gsm8k_glm.yaml` is `gsm8k_cot_llama` with `until: []`, `do_sample: false`, and `max_gen_toks: 16384`.
</details>

`test_pp_stage_sends_tp_reduced_residual_stream` checks that a middle PP stage sends only the TP-reduced residual stream. A tiny-model PP-vs-TP comparison (`tiny-random/glm-5.2` in `tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py`) can't catch this bug, since with dummy weights it passes with or without the fix.

The AMD path gets the same change but this was not tested on ROCm.

## Details

**Root cause.** DSA decoder layers run MLP/MoE with `reduce_results=False`, and the TP all-reduce happens inside the next layer's `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`. The last layer on a non-final PP stage therefore returns `hidden_states` that are a per-TP-rank partial sum. `gpu_worker` sends `IntermediateTensors` with `all_gather_group=get_tp_group()`, which assumes the tensors are identical on every TP rank. TP rank `r` sends only `tensor.reshape(tp, -1)[r]`, and the receiver all-gathers (`isend_tensor_dict` / `irecv_tensor_dict`). With partial sums, the receiver ends up with token chunk `r` holding rank `r`'s partial sum. It then all-reduces again, so chunk `r` becomes `tp × partial_r` instead of `Σ_r partial_r`.

**Fix.** The sending stage sends only `residual + all_reduce(hidden_states)`, which is replicated across TP, so the sliced send stays valid. The receiving stage starts with `residual = None`, so its first layer applies a plain RMSNorm, as it does on the embedding. This matches the old receiver math `fused_allreduce_rms_norm(all_reduce(hidden_states), residual)`.

**Tradeoffs.** The all-reduce moves from the receiving stage to the sending stage, and `residual` is no longer sent, so PP traffic per boundary halves.

**Symptom.** The output stays fluent, so the bug is easy to miss. It shows up as much longer reasoning, repetition loops, and repeated `</think>`.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix]/minicpm ocr downsample mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Pass `downsample_mode` through MiniCPM-OCR image resize when counting visual tokens. transformers 5.21 makes this argument required, and the previous call used the 5.20 signature.

## Claims

- `MiniCPMOcrProcessingInfo._compute_visual_tokens` now passes the image processor's `downsample_mode` to both `find_best_resize` calls and to `get_refine_size`.
- The MiniCPM-OCR processing tests use the same signature, so a missing argument fails the token-count tests.

## Validation
when inferencing or starting server with vllm for [MiniCPM-OCR 1.0](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0), met this error.

```
TypeError: MiniCPMOcrImageProcessor.find_best_resize() missing 1 required positional argument: 'downsample_mode'
```

## Details

Root cause: token counting still called `find_best_resize` and `get_refine_size` as in transformers 5.20. In 5.21 those methods require `downsample_mode`, so placeholder sizing raises `TypeError` before inference. 
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.21/src/transformers/models/minicpm_ocr/image_processing_minicpm_ocr.py#L165-L182

The value passed is `image_processor.downsample_mode` from the processor already pinned for the request, so a per-request override and the checkpoint default stay on the same grid as the pixels.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Budget prefill memory the startup profile misses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill OOMs at `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`: three allocations that grow with the token budget are missed by the startup memory profile. This PR removes or budgets each of them. Fixes #60450.

OOM on a B200 DEP4 prefill instance (`max_model_len` 1M, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, 17 min into an AgentX trace; the same flags at 16384 run for hours):

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB. GPU 2 has a total capacity of
178.35 GiB of which 2.00 GiB is free.
  deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py:625 forward -> attention.py:967 _wq_b_proj
```

The startup plan left 5.31 GiB free; only 2.00 GiB was left at the OOM.

## Changes

| Gap (32768 tokens, 1M context) | Why the profile misses it | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Indexer `expanded_block_table_buffer`: 1 GiB per builder, two builders plus a replay copy | Allocated after KV sizing | Rows = `min(max_num_seqs * next_n, max_num_batched_tokens)`, the decode tokens it serves: 12 MiB |
| Engram layers 1 and 14: `previous_post` (1.25 GiB) held through attention and MoE, plus a 1.75 GiB spike in the call | Skipped in the profile run unless the table is DP-sharded | Profile runs look up dead rows (NVIDIA and AMD models); `del previous_post` after the call |
| Indexer prefill logits: SM100's BF16 output plus its FP32 copy, with the previous chunk's still alive: 2.5x the 512 MiB budget | Reserved at 1x | `del logits` per chunk; the prefill term of the #62860 reservation counts the copy (1.5x) |

No kernel, chunking or scheduling change.

## Validation

- `pre-commit`: pass.
- Unit tests: new `test_indexer_expanded_block_table_sized_by_decode_tokens` (fails on main); `test_engram_dp_shard` updated for dead-row lookups. GPU run pending.
- E2E pending: the same config at 32768 / 0.95, startup KV size and profiled peak, main vs PR.

## Notes

- Decode rows never exceed `max_num_seqs * next_n`: the indexer treats wider requests as prefills, and `build()` asserts the bound with host ints (no sync).
- The dead-row branch runs only without attention metadata (with MRV2, only the profile run), where outputs are discarded.
- Not addressed: the 4.11 GiB reserved-but-unallocated at the OOM (allocator fragmentation).

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Batch-sharded draft logits refactor
commits.pr_body:
## Context

#63554 sharded the draft logits cache under batch-sharded sampling, assigning each request to a rank by its persistent slot: owner `req_state_idx % tp_size`, row `req_state_idx // tp_size`. That ties per-rank load to how the slot allocator happens to spread requests, and it gives each rank a varying number of requests per step. The DSpark follow-up (sharding the sequential Markov block) needs per-rank shapes that are fixed for a given batch size, so it can be CUDA-graph captured.

## This PR

This PR refactors how requests are assigned to ranks, and moves the sharding logic into one object.

**Ownership by batch position.** Every draft step gives the request at batch position `i` to rank `i % tp_size`, at row `i // tp_size` of that rank's cache (`DraftLogitsCache.assign`, called from `DraftModelSpeculator.prepare_propose`). Each rank holds at most `cdiv(num_reqs, tp_size)` requests, however the slots are spread. Verification runs each request on the rank that cached its drafts, via `DraftLogitsCache.owners_of`, which `BatchSharder` uses.

**Reused rows.** Rows are reassigned every step, so a request that the scheduler skips can find its row overwritten. `inverse_row_mapping` records which request last wrote each row. `DraftLogitsCache.stale_drafts` (a Triton kernel) marks drafts whose row has since changed hands, and `RejectionSampler` routes them through the existing invalid-drafts path, so verification resamples from the target. This is lossless: only that step's acceptance drops. **Note that this staleness only affects batch-sharded draft logits.**

**`DraftLogitsCache`** (new, `spec_decode/draft_logits.py`) owns the cache and its mappings:
- `values`: `[num_rows, num_steps, vocab]`;
- `row_mapping`: request slot → row on this rank, or −1;
- `shard_mapping`: request slot → owning rank;
- `inverse_row_mapping`: row → request slot.

The speculator owns it, and `rejection_sample`, `gumbel_sample` and the DFlash2 candidate cache take it, or its `row_mapping`, instead of `num_shards`/`shard_idx` arguments. `draft_logits_row()` is the single lookup: −1 means "no row on this rank", and every writer masks on `row >= 0`. With a replicated cache, `row_mapping` is `None` and every path reduces to indexing by slot. The opt-in rules from #63554 and #64151 are unchanged: the speculator must support it, no draft watermarker, and PCP = 1.

**Balance:** I simulated TP4 with MRv2's LIFO slot allocator and measured the busiest rank's verification load relative to a perfect split.
- Steady load: both rules are within about 1% on average.
- While a burst of 256 requests drains (≤ 64 live), slot ownership averages 1.32× and hits 3.0× worst case. Batch-position ownership averages 1.00×, because it rebalances every step.

## Benchmarks

**Setup:**
- 4× GB200, TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, probabilistic drafting, prefix caching off, natural EOS.
- 4 boots per pair, ordered base, shard, shard, base. "base" has `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` off; "shard" has it on (sharded verification plus the sharded draft logits cache).
- GSM8K: 1319 questions. t0 is temperature 0, one run per boot. t1 is temperature 1, 3 seeds per boot.
- SPEED-Bench: `low_entropy` subset, `throughput_2k` config, temperature 1. Acceptance is measured at c64.
- Latencies are medians.
- Measured on a pre-cleanup revision of this branch. Later changes are renames, docstrings and the rebase; the logic is unchanged.

### Accuracy and acceptance (base → shard)

| Target + draft | GSM8K t0 | GSM8K t1 | AL GSM8K t0 | AL GSM8K t1 | AL SPEED-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP (K=3) | 0.970 → 0.970 | 0.968 → 0.968 | 3.618 → 3.621 | 3.515 → 3.517 | 3.267 → 3.267 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash (K=7) | 0.970 → 0.969 | 0.965 → 0.965 | 5.492 → 5.500 | 4.985 → 4.973 | 3.894 → 3.920 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 (K=7) | 0.964 → 0.963 | 0.960 → 0.960 | 6.164 → 6.157 | 5.890 → 5.893 | 3.646 → 3.649 |

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5) with sharding on had GSM8K accuracy 0.900 at t0 and 0.809 at t1, with acceptance 3.539 and 3.308. That matches the shard numbers in #63554 (0.906 / 0.807 and 3.540 / 3.283).

### Speed, sharding on vs off (median ITL, output tok/s)

| Target + draft | ITL c8 | ITL c64 | ITL c256 | tok/s c64 | tok/s c256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | +2.1% | −5.1% | −8.6% | +3.3% | +6.0% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | +15.4% | −7.6% | −9.5% | +4.0% | +5.5% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | +0.8% | −8.4% | −9.8% | +4.7% | +7.4% |

### Memory, sharding on vs off (from startup logs)

The KV cache gains match #63554: the cache still holds `cdiv(max_num_seqs, tp_size)` rows per rank.

| Target + draft | KV cache memory | KV cache tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 150.69 → 150.95 GiB | +0.17% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 145.77 → 146.39 GiB | +0.43% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 147.07 → 148.31 GiB | +0.85% |

### Notes

- **c8 cost with sharding on.** At c8, step time is bound by rank 0's host work. Per-rank host timers on DFlash at c8 show +1.7 ms of host time per step with sharding on: shard plan 0.35 ms, output gather 0.29 ms, stale-drafts/assign launches about 0.2 ms, and about 0.85 ms not yet attributed. GPU work per step is unchanged. Most of this comes from batch-sharded sampling itself, which already exists on main. The main vs this PR table separates out this PR's share.
- **Not a duplicate.** This refactors the ownership scheme from #63554 and builds on #64151. No other open PR touches this code.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_i64.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py \
  tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py
# 499 passed
```

commits.pr_title: [Fusion] Fuse Qwen MoE shared MLP activation quantization
commits.pr_body:
Related to #43501. Follow-up to [@mgoin's request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43501#issuecomment-5716717828) to roll out manual fusion in model batches.

Route Qwen2MoeMLP through the existing manual activation/quantization fusion. This covers Qwen1.5-MoE, Qwen2-MoE and the reused Qwen3Next MLP, including shared experts. The shared-expert gate still uses the original input.

Native FP8 engagement needs #57514's consumer-key exposure. No kernel or consumer changes are included here.

## Tests

1× H100 80GB, TP1, with nightly binaries:

- Shared-expert FP8 regression: passes with the change, fails without it.
- Qwen2-57B-A14B FP8 with #57514: fusion runs in all 28 shared MLPs. With #59514 too, sampled GSM8K scored 204/256 → 207/256; compiled throughput rose 0.9–1.8% (three runs). Without #59514, throughput was unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][MiniMax-M3] Enable SM90 split-K in the Triton indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Enable the existing MiniMax-M3 indexer split-K path on SM90 with a fixed target of 1056 CTAs. SM120 behavior is unchanged.

## Claims
Fresh validation on h200_agent (2026-10-29): 8×H200, TP8, BF16 real weights, 2048 batched tokens, concurrency 1, random-token prompts, 64 output tokens. TTFT median of 3 runs (min–max in parentheses):

| Input tokens | Baseline, seconds | Split-K, seconds | TTFT reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32,768 | 1.6701 (1.6639–1.6734) | 1.5760 (1.5497–1.5763) | 5.6% |
| 131,072 | 8.7296 (8.7288–8.7438) | 6.5041 (6.5040–6.5149) | 25.5% |
| 229,376 | 18.9614 (18.9611–18.9618) | 12.1225 (12.0730–12.1276) | 36.1% |

## Validation
- Baseline/optimized greedy completion text SHA-256 hashes match at 4K, 32K and 131K inputs (64 output tokens, fixed seeded prompts).
- H200 standalone split-K score checks pass bit-exactly for long-context and mixed-request inputs.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` on both changed files, and `git diff --check` pass; 576 launch-policy combinations checked locally.

Reproduction: serve each arm with `--block-size 128 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len auto`, warm up at 8192 tokens, then issue each input length 3 times. Baseline uses the pre-PR score wrapper; optimized uses b775ed3. Only the indexer score wrapper differs between serving arms; row sharding is disabled in both.

## Details
Chunked prefill underfills Hopper with the unsplit grid. Splits write disjoint score columns. Removed A/B and tuning flags, standalone test scaffolding, and row sharding. Complements #57420 (sparse attention); this change targets indexer scoring. Validation uses the existing v0.31.0 serving environment with the score wrapper overlaid, rather than a full rebuild of current main.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Add a ucx_backend_params key for UCX backend init params
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`NixlConnector` creates NIXL's UCX backend with `num_threads` only, so UCX runs with NIXL's default `ucx_error_handling_mode=peer`. In peer mode UCX wires up only transports that can detect peer failure. On one MI355X node that left tcp: GPU-to-GPU KV reads ran as software emulation over tcp at about 3.4 Gbps, while with `ucx_error_handling_mode=none` UCX picks rocm_ipc zero-copy and a 74 MiB read ran at 483.7 Gbps. `UCX_*` environment variables cannot set this (it is a NIXL backend init parameter), and vLLM has no way to pass one.

## Claims

- New `kv_connector_extra_config.ucx_backend_params` (a dict of strings) passes extra init parameters to the UCX backend. Without the key nothing changes.
- When it is set and UCX is a selected backend, the agent is created with no backends and the worker creates each configured backend itself, in order, with the parameters NIXL would have used; UCX also gets the extra ones. In sleep mode, where the worker already creates UCX itself, the params are added to that call.
- Documented in `docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md` ("UCX backend parameters").

## Validation

Single MI355X node, an equivalent out-of-tree change, one 74 MiB KV read between two GPUs:

| `ucx_error_handling_mode` | UCX transport | throughput |
|---|---|---|
| peer (NIXL default) | tcp | 3.4 Gbps |
| none (`ucx_backend_params`) | rocm_ipc | 483.7 Gbps |

New `test_ucx_backend_params` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py`, 4 cases: no key (the agent config creates the backends, as before); UCX only (created explicitly with `num_threads` and the extra params); UCX + LIBFABRIC (both created in order, params on UCX only); LIBFABRIC only (nothing to apply, nothing changes).

<details>
<summary>commands and output</summary>

Rebased on main `db3b0f0fa`, CPU only:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k test_ucx_backend_params    # with this change
4 passed, 197 deselected, 1 warning in 36.94s

# connector reverted to main
FAILED tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_ucx_backend_params[extra_config1-agent_backends1-created_backends1]
FAILED tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py::test_ucx_backend_params[extra_config2-agent_backends2-created_backends2]
2 failed, 2 passed, 197 deselected, 1 warning in 42.92s
```

Full `test_nixl_connector.py` on main `8e2beaa3b`: 199 passed, 2 failed with the change; 195 passed and the same 2 failed without (`test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[None|ray]`). ruff, typos, SPDX and mypy (3.11 hook) are clean.
</details>

## Details

**Flow.** Only worker start-up changes, on both P and D:

1. `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.__init__` reads `ucx_backend_params` from `kv_connector_extra_config`.
2. Without it: `nixl_agent(..., nixl_agent_config(backends=[...]))` creates the backends, as today.
3. With it and UCX selected: `nixl_agent_config(backends=[])`, then `create_backend(name, params)` for each configured backend in order. UCX gets the params NIXL's agent config would have given it (`num_threads` when UCX is the only backend) plus the extra ones.
4. Memory registration, handshake, and the decode-side read are unchanged; UCX simply selects its transports with the requested error-handling mode, e.g. rocm_ipc instead of tcp within a node.

**Trade-off.** With `ucx_error_handling_mode=none` UCX does not detect a failed peer; the docs section says so. The parameter is opt-in and passed through as given.

**Not tested.** Cross-node transfers with mode none, sleep mode with the params (no unit test), and NVIDIA (cuda_ipc), where we expect the same transport-selection effect but did not measure it.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and this description.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse MXFP8 activation quant into the 1x32 dot_scaled linear for M <= 16
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On gfx950, `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (1x32-scale MXFP8 dense layers: MiniMax-M3/M3.1, ModelOpt/INC MXFP8) runs a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch before every `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. For bf16 activations with 1-16 rows, this PR quantizes the activation inside the GEMM instead, so each such linear is one launch and the output is bit-identical. Fused: K <= 1024 for M <= 16, and K = 2048 for M <= 4.

The fused GEMM quantizes only `min(16, next_pow2(M))` activation rows per K step and repeats them to fill the 16-row MFMA tile; that keeps the per-N-tile quant cost proportional to the real rows and is what makes K = 2048 profitable.

## Claims

- Per-call speedup on MI355X: 1.14x-1.64x for K <= 1024 at M = 1-16, and 1.03x-1.27x for K = 2048 at M = 1-4 (1.15x-1.27x for MiniMax-M3.1 o_proj at TP4, 6144 x 2048). Every other shape and M keeps the existing path (1.00x).
- Output is bitwise equal to the existing path (separate quant + `_select_cfg` tile), including where the fused tile has a different `BLOCK_K`/`BLOCK_N`.
- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4 (on #63232), AgentX concurrency 1: o_proj and shared-expert down_proj run fused with no separate quant launch. Over baseline, in two runs with the arm order swapped: P90 TPOT 1.011x in both, P90 interactivity 1.011-1.012x.
- No change under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, for fp16 activations, for M > 16, for K = 2048 at M > 4, or for K > 2048.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark**: "separate" is `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` + GEMM (current behaviour); "fused" is this PR. Speedup over separate, MI355X:

| shape (N x K) | M=1 | M=2 | M=3 | M=4 | M=5 | M=8 | M=16 | M=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6144 x 384 (M3.1 shared down, TP8) | 1.64x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.47x | 1.45x | 1.01x* |
| 8192 x 512 | 1.48x | 1.49x | 1.49x | 1.51x | 1.44x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 0.99x* |
| 6144 x 768 (M3.1 shared down, TP4) | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.00x* |
| 6144 x 1024 (M3.1 o_proj, TP8) | 1.52x | 1.48x | 1.39x | 1.41x | 1.34x | 1.36x | 1.30x | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 1024 | 1.47x | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.30x | 1.22x | 1.25x | 1.14x | 1.01x* |
| 6144 x 2048 (M3.1 o_proj, TP4) | 1.27x | 1.20x | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 2048 | 1.17x | 1.11x | 1.05x | 1.03x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 2560 x 6144 (M3.1 qkv, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 1536 x 6144 (M3.1 shared gate_up, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |

\* not fused at this shape; the column times the fallback, i.e. the noise floor.

**End to end**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, mono decode off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, on #63232 (`8d0f05a0c`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`) with this PR applied on top; baseline is the same image unchanged. AgentX trace replay (InferenceX), concurrency 1, 600 s per run, `max-num-seqs` 2; run 1 in the order baseline, this PR, run 2 reversed. This PR / baseline (> 1 is better; TPOT as baseline / this PR; P90 interactivity is InferenceX's `intvty.p90` = 1 / P90 TPOT):

| Run | P90 TPOT | P90 interactivity | Total throughput / GPU |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.011x | 1.012x | 1.004x |
| 2 | 1.011x | 1.011x | 1.020x |

GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, full test set, greedy), measured with K <= 1024 fused: baseline 96.51 / this PR 96.21 strict-match (stderr 0.51 / 0.53), within one stderr; vLLM is not batch invariant when requests are batched together, so greedy outputs vary between runs even with bit-identical kernels. The fused output is bitwise equal to the existing path for every tested shape, including K = 2048.

## Details

- **Row trimming.** `BLOCK_M` = 16 is the smallest MFMA tile, but at M < 16 only the first M rows are stored. The kernel takes a constexpr `QUANT_ROWS = min(16, next_pow2(M))`, loads and quantizes that many rows, and repeats them with `broadcast_to` + `reshape`. At `BLOCK_K` = 128 the repeat costs more than the saved quant, so those tiles (K = 384, 640, ...) keep quantizing 16 rows. The unfused path passes `QUANT_ROWS = BLOCK_M` and generates the same code as before.
- **Why only M <= 16, and K = 2048 only up to M = 4.** The fused GEMM requantizes the activation once per N-tile. At small M the separate launch (plus the round trip of the fp8 activation and its scales) dominates; with more rows or larger K the redundant quant work wins (table above). The gate does not look at N; cutting K = 2048 at M = 4 keeps every measured N at or above 1.03x.
- **`K` becomes a `tl.constexpr`.** Without it the fused loop is not unrolled/pipelined and the fused GEMM is ~0.8x even at K = 512. #63232 makes the same change.
- **Compiles.** Triton already specializes M on `== 1` and `% 16 == 0`; `QUANT_ROWS` adds up to three more variants per fused shape (6 instead of 3 for M = 1-16 at `BLOCK_K` >= 256; 5 at K = 2048, where M = 5-16 stays unfused). For MiniMax-M3.1 at TP4 that is 17 instead of 12 `_mxfp8_linear_kernel` compiles over M = 1-16 (15 instead of 12 at TP8). They are compiled in the eager warm-up before CUDA graph capture; vLLM's capture sizes include every M from 1 to 16, so decode never compiles at runtime, and graph capture time was unchanged in the end-to-end runs.
- **bf16 only.** The in-kernel fp8 cast makes the compiler enable the FP16 overflow clamp in the MODE register for the whole kernel, so an fp16 output that overflows saturates at +-65504 where the unfused GEMM produces inf. bf16 output is unaffected and bit-identical; fp16 activations keep the separate quant.
- **Batch invariance.** Fused and unfused use different tiles (and therefore K-reduction orders), so under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#52231) every M stays on the unfused path.
- **Limitations.** Only gfx950 (`dot_scaled` path). Shapes are tuned on MI355X.

---

commits.pr_title: [Models] Deprecate `torch.compile` for Qwen3.5 models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Qwen3.5 dropped `@support_torch_compile` in favor of breakable CUDA graphs (`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH`, auto-enabled in `vllm/config/vllm.py`). An isolation experiment (same old code, compile vs breakable cudagraph) showed the removal alone cost **+45 ~ 64% decode-step and +22 ~ 39% prefill latency**. This change recovers the lost inductor fusions with explicit fused kernels, ending **5~11% faster than the torch.compile baseline** on decode and at parity on prefill.

## Claims

- End-to-end serving (`vllm bench serve`, up to 128 concurrent requests): decode ITL **-3.0% ~ -8.8%**, prefill TTFT **-7.0% ~ -8.9%** vs the torch.compile baseline (9B + 35B-A3B).
- Isolated forward latency (`vllm bench latency`): decode step **-4.9% ~ -10.7%**, MTP decode **-17% ~ -38%**, prefill at parity.
- Greedy decoding output is **token-identical** to the torch.compile baseline (TP1 and TP2).

## Validation

Environment: 1x NVIDIA GB200 (SM100, aarch64) per run, bf16, real weights (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` dense, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` MoE). Baseline = pre-removal commit (`44e88ae582^`) with default `VLLM_COMPILE`; "old+breakable" = same commit with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1`; "this PR" = HEAD with all fusions. Note: newer vLLM defaults prefix caching ON, which alone inflated TTFT by ~17-20% in an unnormalized run — both trees below use identical serving flags to avoid that artifact.

### End-to-end serving (vllm serve + vllm bench serve, random dataset)

Both trees with identical serving flags (`--no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192`; note newer vLLM defaults prefix caching ON, which alone inflated TTFT by ~17-20% in an unnormalized run — flagged here so reviewers don't reproduce that artifact). Load: 320/384/512 prompts (10+ waves) for concurrency 32/64/128 decode, 128 prompts for the 4k-context decode, 16 prompts for single-stream decode and prefill; output 256 tokens (decode) / 8 tokens (prefill), `--ignore-eos`.

| Model | case | metric | baseline (compile) | this PR | Δ | output throughput Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9B | decode cc=32 | Mean ITL | 4.84 ms | **4.50 ms** | **-7.0%** | +38.0% |
| 9B | decode cc=64 | Mean ITL | 5.59 ms | **5.25 ms** | **-6.1%** | +7.3% |
| 9B | decode cc=128 | Mean ITL | 7.36 ms | **6.90 ms** | **-6.2%** | +6.2% |
| 9B | decode cc=32, 4k ctx | Mean ITL | 8.89 ms | **8.52 ms** | **-4.2%** | +4.1% |
| 9B | single-stream decode | Mean ITL | 4.16 ms | **3.92 ms** | **-5.8%** | +7.3% |
| 9B | 4k-token prefill | Mean TTFT | 74.50 ms | **67.84 ms** | **-8.9%** | +8.4% |
| 35B-A3B | decode cc=32 | Mean ITL | 8.41 ms | **8.03 ms** | **-4.5%** | +5.7% |
| 35B-A3B | decode cc=64 | Mean ITL | 11.02 ms | **10.58 ms** | **-4.0%** | +4.2% |
| 35B-A3B | decode cc=128 | Mean ITL | 14.09 ms | **13.67 ms** | **-3.0%** | +2.7% |
| 35B-A3B | decode cc=32, 4k ctx | Mean ITL | 12.04 ms | **11.39 ms** | **-5.4%** | +5.4% |
| 35B-A3B | single-stream decode | Mean ITL | 3.52 ms | **3.21 ms** | **-8.8%** | +10.4% |
| 35B-A3B | 4k-token prefill | Mean TTFT | 104.02 ms | **96.74 ms** | **-7.0%** | +8.4% |

The gap narrows at higher concurrency (compute-bound regime, fusion matters less) but never inverts; PR-side numbers were measured on the merged tree (upstream/main `fc47cc8fff`), with post-merge `vllm bench latency` spot checks matching pre-merge within noise (9B decode bs1 3.94 vs 3.93 ms).

### Isolated forward latency (vllm bench latency, decode step = (latency[output=65] - latency[output=1]) / 64)

| Model | bs | baseline (compile) | old+breakable | HEAD (no fixes) | this PR | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9B | 1 | 4.20 ms | 6.07 (+44.5%) | 5.48 (+30.5%) | **3.93 ms** | **-6.6%** |
| 9B | 32 | 4.97 ms | 7.83 (+57.3%) | 6.93 (+39.3%) | **4.50 ms** | **-9.6%** |
| 35B-A3B (MoE) | 1 | 3.39 ms | 5.56 (+64.0%) | 4.98 (+47.1%) | **3.03 ms** | **-10.7%** |
| 35B-A3B (MoE) | 32 | 7.58 ms | 11.17 (+47.5%) | 10.03 (+32.4%) | **7.21 ms** | **-4.9%** |

MTP (`--speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`), decode step ms, 9B: bs1 4.91 → **4.07 (-17.2%)**; bs32 8.98 → **5.58 (-37.8%)**.

### Prefill forward (wall seconds, vllm bench latency)

| Model | case | baseline (compile) | old+breakable | HEAD (no fixes) | this PR | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9B | 4096tok x1 | 0.0553 | 0.0734 (+32.7%) | 0.0703 (+27.1%) | **0.0537** | **-2.9%** |
| 9B | 4096tok x8 | 0.3835 | 0.5065 (+32.1%) | 0.4840 (+26.2%) | **0.3802** | **-0.9%** |
| 35B-A3B | 4096tok x1 | 0.0802 | 0.0975 (+21.6%) | 0.0915 (+14.1%) | 0.0829 | +3.4% |
| 35B-A3B | 4096tok x8 | 0.2736 | 0.3802 (+39.0%) | 0.3620 (+32.3%) | **0.2722** | **-0.5%** |

### Correctness

- Kernel unit tests (GB200, via Slurm): **245 passed** (`test_fused_sigmoid_gate_mul.py`, `test_gemma_rms_norm_triton.py`, `test_fused_pre_fc_norms.py`, `test_gdn_qwen35_strided_inputs.py` — the GDN strided/fused-norm paths are asserted bit-exact vs the contiguous/reference kernels).
- End-to-end greedy smoke (9B, 4 prompts x 64 tokens): **token-identical** to the torch.compile baseline at TP1, and TP2 (exercises the fused all-reduce+RMSNorm path) matches TP1 exactly.
- `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_5_quantization.py`: 4 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff, mypy, SPDX, test-tethering).

### Reproduce

```bash
# E2E serving (per tree, per model) — full commands in ~/e2e_qwen35_sbatch.sh
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --port 8192 &
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8192 --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 32 --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256   # decode cc=32 (also: 384@cc64, 512@cc128, 128@cc32 with input 4096)
vllm bench serve ... --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256    # decode single-stream
vllm bench serve ... --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 8    # prefill TTFT

# Isolated forward latency (per tree, per model) — full commands in ~/bench_qwen35_sbatch.sh
vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --num-iters-warmup 2 --num-iters 5 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --input-len 4096 --output-len 1 --batch-size 1     # prefill
vllm bench latency ... --input-len 32 --output-len 1 --batch-size 1     # decode t(1)
vllm bench latency ... --input-len 32 --output-len 65 --batch-size 1    # decode t(65); step = (t65-t1)/64
vllm bench latency ... --input-len 32 --output-len {1,65} --batch-size 32

# MTP decode — ~/mtp_bench_qwen35_sbatch.sh
vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' --input-len 32 --output-len {1,65} --batch-size {1,32} ...

# Kernel unit tests — ~/ktest_qwen35_sbatch.sh
python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_sigmoid_gate_mul.py tests/kernels/core/test_gemma_rms_norm_triton.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_pre_fc_norms.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_qwen35_strided_inputs.py -q

# Greedy-output smoke (TP1/TP2) — ~/smoke_qwen35_sbatch.sh + ~/smoke_qwen35.py
python ~/smoke_qwen35.py Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B <tp> out.json   # LLM(..., tensor_parallel_size=tp), temperature=0, 64 tokens x 4 prompts
```

AI assistance: this change was developed with AI-agent assistance; every benchmark and test command above was actually run on the listed hardware, and all results are reproducible from the referenced logs.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Enable ROCm AITER unified attention for MiMo-V2.6
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

MiMo-V2.6 has asymmetric K/V head dims (192 / 128), which today pins it to the DiffKV attention backends: any other `--attention-backend` is silently replaced by the DiffKV auto-pick, and the native KV-cache write would copy V with K's head width. This PR makes `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` usable for the model (opt-in, defaults unchanged) and fixes the write kernel.

## Claims

- `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` now selects unified attention for every MiMo-V2.6 layer instead of being dropped; verified on Flash (TP2, TP4, TP8) and on Pro (TP8, gsm8k n=100 parity).
- `reshape_and_cache_flash` writes V with its own head size and head stride. Symmetric callers run the same code as before: the new checks live in the asymmetric branch, and the existing kernel is byte-identical to `main`.
- Accuracy and speculative-decoding parity with the default backend (gsm8k at n=1319, MTP x3 acceptance).
- At long context prefill is 1.43x faster at 128k and 1.21x at 32k, with decode 1.17x faster per token (TPOT p50 2.94 vs 3.45 ms) and output throughput up 21-45%. At 8k with concurrency 8 the two are at parity. Measured with `--block-size 16` on both arms, which tested better than the backend's default for this shape. On Pro at TP8 the same benchmark gives 1.13x prefill and 1.66x lower inter-token latency.

## Validation

### Commands

```bash
# serve (TP4 shown; TP2/TP8 differ only in --tensor-parallel-size; the control arm drops
# --attention-backend and gets the DiffKV auto-pick)
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 270336 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 \
  --block-size 16 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

# serve bench, one cell (input/output lengths and prompt counts per the tables)
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 1 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

# gsm8k 25-shot against the running server
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

# tests
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py
```

### Bench serve

Mimo-V2.6 Flash at TP4:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 7633.8 ms | 5317.7 ms | -30% (1.44x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 4.10 tok/s | 5.96 tok/s | +45% |
| 32k in / 128 out, 4 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 890.9 ms | 738.2 ms | -17% (1.21x) |
| 32k in / 128 out: TPOT p50 | 3.45 ms | 2.94 ms | -15% |
| 32k in / 128 out: output throughput | 96.1 tok/s | 116.0 tok/s | +21% |
| 8k in / 256 out, 8 prompts, c8: ITL p50 | 8.42 ms | 8.48 ms | parity |
| 8k in / 256 out: output throughput | 929 tok/s | 947 tok/s | +2% |

On MiMo-V2.6-Pro at TP8:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 9665.0 ms | 8576.9 ms | -11% (1.13x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: ITL p50 | 19.52 ms | 11.77 ms | -40% (1.66x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 3.23 tok/s | 3.68 tok/s | +14% |

Acceptance rate:
| | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified |
|---|---|---|
| MTP acceptance, 128k (acc % / length) | 53.33 / 2.07 | 56.67 / 2.13 |
| MTP acceptance, 32k | 61.40 / 2.23 | 55.60 / 2.11 |
| MTP acceptance, 8k c8 | 57.4-60.5 | 58.2-60.3 |


### lm_eval

| checkpoint | unified | DiffKV | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash, gsm8k n=1319 | 0.9750 / 0.9742 | 0.9719 / 0.9712 | strict / flexible |

### Needle-In-A-Haystack

Unified attention only; `--max-model-len 270336`, thinking off, greedy.

| probe | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| niah | 265,673 tokens, depths 0 / 50 / 100 % | 3/3 |

### Tests

```
# kernel fix: main's cache_kernels.cu vs this one
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric        # 33 failed -> 33 passed
# model change: main's backend selection vs this one (either kernel)
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py             # 2 failed, 5 passed -> 7 passed
```

The asymmetric kernel test runs MiMo's geometry (K 192 / V 128, 4 KV heads) at both block sizes the model uses (16 and 64) over a parametrized token count, in both layouts unified attention hands the kernel, for bf16 and fp8 caches and per-tensor and per-head scales. The whole file stays green (694 passed, 602 skipped).

The model test gained two checks: the selected backend's *impl* has to be unified attention's, not just its enum; and the cache the layer writes has to match a cache built in torch, per slot, with K in the first `head_dim` columns of a row and V in the remaining `v_head_dim`. Both fail on `main`. The kernel test's buffers carry slack past the cache, so a regressed kernel fails that comparison instead of writing out of bounds.

## Details

`reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` derived one head size, one page stride, one head stride and one element count from key/key_cache and reused all of them for the value side:

```cpp
cache_t* v_dst_h = value_dst + head * head_stride;             // K's stride
vectorize_with_alignment(value_src, value_dst, n_elems, ...);  // K's width
```

Every caller until now was symmetric, so this was invisible. Unified attention is the first caller that passes `v_head_size != head_size` (MiMo is 192 / 128, packed as one `(head_size + head_size_v)` content dim per KV head), and for it V was read at K's per-head offset, copied at K's width - 64 elements past the end of each head - and written past the end of the cache on the last slot. The asymmetric case now gets its own kernel that addresses V with the value side's own head stride and length; the existing kernel and its NHD fast path are untouched, so symmetric callers run the same code as before.

Model side: the attention backend is chosen per layer, and the gate now consults a backend capability (`supports_head_size_v`) rather than listing backend names. DiffKV declares that it can serve any K/V width relation; unified attention declares `v <= k`, because it splits the page with `split(head_size)`. A backend that cannot serve the shape still gets the previous behaviour: a warning and the DiffKV auto-pick.

Known limitations:

- Requires aiter >= 0.1.25 for the V-dim-masked unified-attention kernels; `main` pins 0.1.26.
- Unified attention serves V narrower than K, not wider (`v_head_dim > head_dim` cannot be expressed by its page split); such a request falls back to the DiffKV auto-pick with a warning.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NVFP4] Fix NaN logits and garbage output from uninitialized fused act+quant scales
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make the fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel initialize the padded entries of the swizzled NVFP4 block-scale buffer, as the unfused `scaled_fp4_quant` kernel already does. Fixes a regression from #53568, which switched the scale allocator to `torch.empty` (previously `torch.zeros`, restored in #45739).

## Claims

- Fixes NaN logits and garbage output (`other other other ...`) on NVFP4 checkpoints, e.g. `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`.
- Fixes HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan` on `/v1/chat/completions` with `logprobs`.
- Covers both users of the kernel (the `ActivationQuantFusionPass` and the manual fusion in `fused_act_quant.py`) with no allocator memset.

## Validation

Setup: 8x RTX PRO 4500 (sm120), TP=8, `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4`, FlashInfer-Cutlass NVFP4 linear backend, `fuse_act_quant: True`, built from source with CUDA 13.2.

Repro:

```bash
# 1. Serve (TP=8)
vllm serve nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --served-model-name nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5 --port 8000

# 2. Once the server is up, send 100 chat+logprobs and 100 completions requests
NAME=nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1.5
echo -n "chat:  "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_chat_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"logprobs\":true,\"top_logprobs\":1,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a helpful assistant.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello!\"}],\"max_tokens\":100}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo -n "compl: "; for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /tmp/r_compl_$i.json -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"model\":\"$NAME\",\"prompt\":\"What is the test plan?\",\"logprobs\":2,\"max_tokens\":50,\"temperature\":0}"; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' '; echo
echo "nan-errors: $(grep -l 'Out of range float' /tmp/r_*.json | wc -l)"
```

Unit tests: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`, 20 passed (12 existing, 8 new).

## Details

The fused `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant` kernel only wrote valid rows of the swizzled block-scale buffer, but the NVFP4 GEMM reads the padded entries, so since #53568 switched the allocator to `torch.empty` it consumed stale memory as scales and produced NaN logits. This PR makes the kernel zero the padded scale rows and columns itself (as `scaled_fp4_quant` does) and keeps the allocators as `torch.empty`, so there is no extra memset.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Qwen4Exp] Enable fp8 KV and indexer caches on the AMD QSA path
commits.pr_body:
## Summary On AMD GPUs, two vLLM flags that enable 8-bit (fp8) KV caching did not work for Qwen4Exp models. This PR makes both flags work. Users get ~33% more KV cache capacity at 16K context with no quality change outside the eval noise. Peak batch throughput at concurrency 16 is ~6% lower; single-request speed is unchanged. Both flags are opt-in. ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 ... \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 ``` `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` shrinks the main KV cache; `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8` shrinks the compressed-key cache of the model's sparse indexer (QSA). The indexer's raw state cache stays bf16. AMD has two fp8 encodings — FNUZ on gfx942 (MI300) and OCP on gfx950 (MI355) — and the caches use the platform's native one. ## Claims - **Capacity:** +33% at tensor-parallel size 1 (TP1) and 16K context with both flags (2,505,113 → 3,336,874 tokens); the main KV cache halves. Measured on the pre-merge head (`87b62b06e8`). Capacity comparisons are same-max-model-len only. - **Quality:** neutral on GSM8K 5-shot (strict 0.899 vs 0.902; flexible 0.881 vs 0.895, with overlapping run ranges), within the binomial error on GPQA-Diamond (0.4747 vs 0.4596), and identical long-context retrieval (90/90 NIAH cells). - **Deterministic gates:** greedy outputs are byte-identical to the bf16 baseline (a 391-token arithmetic prompt ×3 and a France→Paris continuation at temperature 0). - **Tradeoff:** single-request decode is unchanged; concurrency-16 aggregate throughput is ~6% lower with both flags. The flags are opt-in, a capacity-vs-concurrency choice. ## Validation ### Unit tests `pytest -v tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → **55 passed** on MI355X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.2). The same suite runs on the new MI300 CI step (gfx942/FNUZ); that leg is the regression guard for the gfx942-only scale fix and is pending a full CI run on this head. The prepare test compares the fused Triton kernel's stored fp8 codes against the C++ `reshape_and_cache_flash` reference, using separate contiguous uint8 buffers and the same 0.5/2.0 scales. Both paths write the platform's native flavor, so the C++ op is a valid unfused reference on both arches. The sparse-attention test is parametrized over bf16 and platform fp8; its reference consumes the quantized cache upcast to float, directly exercising the new fp8 read path.
Red run: the fp8 scale fix reverted (historical capture) The original red capture (`fe6ad8c6`, 2026-10-13) was on gfx950/MI355X with the fp8 destination **explicitly typed as FNUZ**. The pre-fix condition (`out_ty == tl.float8e4nv`) already matched OCP, so FNUZ typing was needed to expose the bug on OCP-native hardware. 8 cells failed (fp8 main × bf16 indexer); 16 were skipped because indexer-fp8 combinations were unsupported then. ``` FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[text-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-model-1d-indexer_dtype0-True] ... (8 total) ============ 8 failed, 8 passed, 16 skipped, 14 warnings in 11.37s ============ ``` The stored/expected code differences are a systematic ~8 code steps across the whole cache — exactly the `k_scale=0.5` mis-scale — far outside the tolerance (`code_diff <= 2 | abs_diff <= RTOL*|expected| + 2*ATOL`). The current test parametrizes the platform dtype. On gfx950 the fp8 cells are OCP, which the pre-fix condition already handled; the 16 `main_fp8=True` cells reproduce on the gfx942/MI300 leg. That leg is why the MI300 CI step was added.
Pre-change boot failures with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 ``` NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache # impl + layer + backend gates NotImplementedError: FlashAttention does not support fp8 kv-cache on this device. # FA base check ```
Green at the current head ``` ======================= 55 passed, 14 warnings in 21.78s ======================= ``` `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → 23 passed. `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/ --ignore=tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → 186 passed, 86 skipped (pre-merge baseline; not re-run after the upstream merges). Whole-directory collection has a pre-existing custom-op registration clash, reproducible on the clean tree.
### Throughput Decode is unchanged; peak concurrency throughput is ~6% lower with both flags. The flags are opt-in and independent, so the indexer cache can be enabled alone at no measurable throughput cost.
Throughput numbers ``` decode, 7K context / 512 output tokens: bf16 baseline: 111.0-111.5 tok/s both fp8: 110.5-110.6 tok/s concurrency-16 aggregate: bf16 baseline: 508.4-510.1 tok/s (3 runs) indexer fp8: 509.1-512.1 tok/s (3 runs) main KV fp8: 491.7-510.3 tok/s (3 runs) both fp8: 464-485 tok/s (6 runs, two host-load levels) ```
### Capacity Table at 16K context, TP1, MI355X, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` (AMD's AITER kernels), max-num-seqs 16, no multi-token prediction (MTP), on the pre-merge head (`87b62b06e8`): | config | GPU KV cache (tokens) | greedy gates | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline | 2,505,113 | 391 ×3, France→Paris exact | | indexer fp8 | 2,541,158 (+1.5%) | identical | | main KV fp8 | 3,238,570 (+29.3%) | identical | | both | **3,336,874 (+33.2%)** | identical | At 32K context (the GPQA/NIAH eval config), the pre-merge head held 5,005,312 tokens (vs 3,336,874 at 16K, +49.9%); a post-merge boot with both flags held 5,062,656 (+1.1% vs the pre-merge 32K number). The shift comes from the upstream merge set and was not bisected. The current head includes a further upstream merge, so its 32K capacity is not re-measured. Capacity comparisons are same-max-model-len only; the +33% headline is at 16K. At tensor-parallel size 4 (TP4; cards 4–7, same protocol), the indexer-fp8 gain grows because the indexer side cache is replicated (`num_kv_heads=1`) while the main KV shards: 11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens (+3.05%, vs +1.5% at TP1). The FP8 checkpoint at TP4 on this tree needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce`; the open #60839 adds automatic fallbacks for both.
Raw boot-log lines (16K) ``` bf16: GPU KV cache size: 2,505,113 tokens indexer fp8: GPU KV cache size: 2,541,158 tokens main KV fp8: GPU KV cache size: 3,238,570 tokens both: GPU KV cache size: 3,336,874 tokens ```
### Quality All quality numbers are from pre-merge measurements (the same build within each comparison), TP1, MI355X. GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, 250-problem deterministic subset, 6 runs per config, lm-evaluation-harness against the served endpoint: | config | flexible-extract (6 runs) | mean | strict-match (6 runs) | mean | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 | 0.900 0.888 0.908 0.884 0.900 0.892 | 0.895 | 0.888 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.908 | 0.902 | | indexer fp8 | 0.900 0.892 0.876 0.892 0.884 0.896 | 0.890 | 0.908 0.896 0.884 0.916 0.884 0.912 | 0.900 | | both fp8 | 0.892 0.884 0.868 0.876 0.884 0.880 | 0.881 | 0.896 0.904 0.896 0.884 0.904 0.908 | 0.899 | Strict-match is neutral; flexible-extract is −1.4 points with fully overlapping ranges. GPQA-Diamond and needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) long-context retrieval, both arms on the pre-merge head, TP1, MI355X, max-model-len 32768, greedy temperature 0: | arm | GPQA-Diamond flexible-extract (198 q) | NIAH ({8,16,32}K × depths {0,25,50,75,100}% × 2 needles × 3 seeds) | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 (auto) | 0.4596 ± 0.0355 | 90/90 = 100% | | fp8 main + indexer | 0.4747 ± 0.0356 | 90/90 = 100% | GPQA is within the binomial standard error (fp8 nominally +1.5 points). Strict-match is 0.00 in both arms (a chain-of-thought answer-format artifact); flexible-extract is the paired metric. NIAH retrieval is perfect in both arms at every (length, depth) cell — fp8 indexer scores and fp8 main KV preserve long-context retrieval identically up to 32K.
Raw GSM8K score lines (first two runs per config) ``` bf16: |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.900|± |0.019| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.888|± |0.0200| both fp8:|gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.892|± |0.0197| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.884|± |0.0203| ```
### Post-merge regression check After the Octave KV (#59774) and later Qwen4Exp merges, a boot with both fp8 flags is healthy: the QSA backend is selected with no Octave interference, the 32K capacity is the number above, and the greedy gates (391 ×3 and France→Paris) are byte-identical to the pre-merge head. The quality evals above were not re-run post-merge. ## Limitations / known gaps - **Unit KV scales only.** The fp8 main KV cache requires unit per-tensor scales (the default). The layer rejects a checkpoint `kv_cache_scheme`, and `forward_qsa` raises `NotImplementedError` if the runtime `_k_scale_float`/`_v_scale_float` are not 1.0. The Triton kernel casts fp8 K to the query dtype and V to fp16 without multiplying by the scale. The NVIDIA port's host-side dequant fold is the follow-up if calibrated scales matter. - **No serve-level gfx942 run.** Unit and kernel tests cover gfx942/FNUZ; the serving, capacity, and quality numbers are MI355X/OCP. A full gfx942 serve run has not been performed. - **Concurrency tradeoff.** Concurrency-16 aggregate is ~6% lower with both flags; decode is unchanged. Both flags are opt-in. ## Details
What changed (three logical changes, plus review fixups) 1. **Fix the fp8 scale divide for FNUZ destinations.** On gfx942 the fp8 cache is FNUZ (`tl.float8e4b8`); on gfx950 it is OCP (`tl.float8e4nv`). `_to_dst_dtype` divided by the KV scale only for OCP, so FNUZ destinations skipped the divide. With the unit scales this path requires today, dividing by 1.0 is a no-op; the fix matters if calibrated KV scales are supported. The test uses 0.5/2.0 scales to exercise the divide. 2. **Support `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`.** Wires `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype` through `amd/indexer_qsa.py`, mirroring the NVIDIA reference. The compressed-key cache and the query-side cast use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()`; the raw state cache stays bf16. The fused kernel already handled fp8-typed stores and loads; the wiring and test coverage were missing. 3. **Support fp8 main KV cache.** Lifts the dtype gates and interprets the uint8 main cache in the platform's native flavor at the typed boundaries. The sparse-attention kernel gains an `IS_FP8` constexpr (K upcast to the query dtype for the QK dot; V to fp16 for the PV dot). The QSA implementation passes `"auto"` to the FlashAttention base class for its fp8-support probe and restores the real dtype afterwards, mirroring NVIDIA; the backend's combination check delegates with no fp8 dtype, so only that probe is bypassed while the other checks remain. `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` is honored per layer. The QSA cache dtype list now covers fp8 alongside the Octave formats (#59774).
Flavor design and the C++ reference AMD has two fp8 encodings: FNUZ on gfx942 (MI300) and OCP on gfx950 (MI355). The main cache is allocated as uint8 and reinterpreted with `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` in the fused prepare, the attention read, and the C++ cache-update path. The C++ `reshape_and_cache_flash` follows the platform flavor (verified on gfx950: 1.0 → 0x38 and -1.0 → 0xb8, i.e. OCP; FNUZ would encode 1.0 as 0x40). The test therefore uses the C++ op as the unfused reference, with separate contiguous uint8 buffers and the same scales.
Cross-arch and TP4 notes Validated end-to-end on gfx950/MI355X. The gfx942/FNUZ leg is unit/kernel-test validated; a serve-level gfx942 run has not been performed. At TP4, the indexer side cache is replicated while the main KV shards, so the indexer-fp8 capacity gain grows from +1.5% at TP1 to +3.05% (11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens); the absolute gain scales ~9×. The TP4 FP8 checkpoint needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` on this tree; the open #60839 adds automatic fallbacks for both.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Parenthesize penalties Triton chained `or` for Ascend backends
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #64046

**One-line:** Ascend Triton cannot lower chained boolean `or` in V1 `_penalties_kernel` (`A or B or C` → `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct`). The first request with non-default sampling penalties can kill the TP worker group / EngineCore. This PR parenthesizes into binary `or`s. CUDA Triton semantics unchanged.

---

## What broke (feature)

This is the OpenAI-compatible **sampling penalty** path (`repetition_penalty` / `frequency_penalty` / `presence_penalty`), **not** MTP / EPLB / MDRv2 / KV pool. Those may be enabled in the same deployment but are unrelated to the compiler failure.

---

## Environment where we hit it

| Item | Value |
|------|--------|
| Hardware | Ascend A3 NPU |
| Deploy | PD disagg **4P8–1D8**, 505B W4A8, Ascend Triton |
| Path | `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/penalties.py` → `_penalties_kernel` |
| Trigger | **First** request with non-default penalties (lazy JIT) |
| Incidents | 2026-10-24 14:35 (p0), 2026-10-26 22:34 (p1, `Worker_TP13`) |

Traffic without penalties can look healthy for a long time; sibling nodes on the same build are latent until they see a penalty request.

---

## Claims

- Removes Ascend Triton’s **chained-`or` AST** failure for `_penalties_kernel`.
- No intended behavior change on CUDA.
- Does **not** claim to fix every Ascend follow-on (BiShengIR / UB tile, missing `aclnnRightShift` in alternate torch paths). Those stay in NPU plugins / stack work.
- Not duplicating an open upstream PR for this AST issue (searched `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct` / chained boolean).

---

## Key error log (production)

```text
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/penalties.py", line 200, in apply_penalties
    _penalties_kernel[(num_tokens, num_blocks)](
...
File ".../triton/backends/ascend/__init__.py", ... in _patched_make_ir
...
triton.compiler.errors.UnsupportedLanguageConstruct: at 26:18:
    use_penalty = use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty or use_pres_penalty
                  ^
chained boolean operators (A or B or C) are not supported; use parentheses to split the chain.

WorkerProc hit an exception.
EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

Abbreviated call chain:

```text
worker_busy_loop → sample_tokens → sampler.apply_sampling_params
  → apply_penalties → _penalties_kernel JIT → Ascend ast_to_ttir → boom
```

---

## Root cause / fix

| Layer | Status in this PR |
|-------|-------------------|
| L1 chained `or` | **Fixed** via parentheses |
| L2 BiShengIR / tile after parens | Out of scope (downstream) |
| L3 torch `>>` / RightShift gaps | Out of scope (downstream) |

```python
# before
use_penalty = use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty or use_pres_penalty

# after
use_penalty = (use_rep_penalty or use_freq_penalty) or use_pres_penalty
```

Ascend’s own error text recommends splitting the chain with parentheses.

---

## Validation

**Outside CI (Ascend NPU, production-like PD):**
- Repro: chat/completions with e.g. `repetition_penalty=1.1` (+ optional freq/pres).
- Before: `UnsupportedLanguageConstruct` on chained `or`, then worker/Engine death.
- After parentheses: this specific AST error is gone on stacks that only needed L1.

**CI / tests:**
- No new unit test: failure requires Ascend Triton; default CUDA CI cannot exercise it (documented resource constraint).
- Expect existing CUDA sampling / penalties paths to keep passing.

**Limitation:** some Ascend builds may still fail later (L2). NPU plugins may additionally shrink `BLOCK_SIZE` or ship a torch fallback (see omniinfer [#3147](https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3147) merged Triton adapt / [#3148](https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3148) torch exploration); that does not replace making upstream source AST-safe.

---

## Details / tradeoffs

- Tiny readability change; no CUDA perf impact expected.
- Keeps one shared kernel instead of forking Ascend-only source in core.
- **Merged NPU-plugin fix (same L1):** https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3147 — Ascend-compatible MRv2 penalty kernel writing + UT (merged). This upstream PR mirrors the L1 parentheses part into vLLM `main`.
- Alternate NPU torch rewrite (L2/L3 context, closed): https://gitee.com/omniai/omniinfer/pulls/3148

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Allow DSpark adaptive verification with DCP on ROCM_AITER_MLA
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#59824 enabled DSpark adaptive verification (AV) on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` for `decode_context_parallel_size == 1` only. Kimi-K3 on MI355X serves its mid- and high-concurrency points at TP8/DCP8, where AV was refused after the weight load. This PR enables AV at DCP > 1 on the routes that place verify queries by global position (cprr asm, segmented MLA, gfx942 Triton).

## Claims

- AV produces exact attention at DCP > 1 on the cprr and segmented routes (unit level with real kernels; see Validation).
- Every kernel input stays exactly as in uniform DCP verify: local and global lengths, `g_kv_indptr`, page indices, no `CLAMP_TAIL`. Only the q/o row maps change; unlike DCP1 there is no extra page-index buffer for padded lengths.
- An AV + DCP configuration that no route can serve now fails at backend selection, before the weights load, instead of in the AV manager after the load.
- DCP1 behaviour is unchanged.

## Validation

All runs on MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-e68efc685ab1`, AITER 0.1.25.

**New GPU test** (`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py::test_adaptive_varlen_shards_match_reference`, cprr and segmented). It runs the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.build` and the real kernels, with the 8 DCP ranks simulated one after another on one GPU, as the existing cprr test does.
- **Shape:** Kimi-K3's verify shape: 96 gathered heads padded to 128, W = 5.
- **Batch:** ragged device admitted lengths behind an even host split. It includes a single token, a full block, sequences shorter than the block and than DCP, cudagraph dummy requests, and token padding past the last request.
- **Per shard:** the output and LSE must match an exact torch reference with causality on global positions.
- **Merge:** the raw shards go through the production `correct_attn_out` over `mask_dcp_empty_shards_`-masked LSEs. The merged output must be finite and must match full-context attention.

**New CPU tests** (`tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`):
- **`test_varlen_cudagraph_bound_follows_adaptive_verification` (extended):** covers the gate with DCP8, interleave 2, W = 2 and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=segmented`.
- **`test_backend_rejects_unsupported_adaptive_dcp`:** `validate_configuration` raises.
- **`test_dcp_varlen_right_aligns_rows_and_keeps_lengths`:** the right-aligned q/o row maps, the unchanged local and global lengths, and `CLAMP_TAIL` off.

**Mutation check.** Each of the following mutants fails at least one of these tests:
- right-align disabled, or a shift off by one;
- the seq-len pad re-applied at DCP, or `CLAMP_TAIL` always on;
- the LSE gather dropped (GPU test only);
- the `row_pos >= 0` term removed;
- in the gate: always passing, no interleave check, no `W >= 3` term, no `segmented` env clause;
- the `validate_configuration` hook removed.

**Regression**, this branch vs `main` (70a609ac40) on the same image:

| Suite | branch | main |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_{mtp_split,dcp_cprr,dcp_cprr_numerics,dcp_verify_gfx942,fp8_decode_routing}.py` | 577 passed, 7 skipped | 573 passed, 7 skipped |
| `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_adaptive_verification.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py` | 122 passed | 122 passed |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k "aiter or AITER or varlen or adaptive or ragged"` (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`) | 581 passed | 581 passed |

Reproduce:
```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py   # numerics need gfx950
```

## Details

**Why the DCP1 layout is wrong under DCP.** Under AV, the host `query_start_loc_cpu` holds an even split of the draft budget, and the device `query_start_loc` holds each request's admitted length q ≤ W = K + 1. At DCP1, #59824 runs every request as a uniform W-row block:
- Real tokens are left-aligned.
- The kernel KV length is extended by the pad `W - q`.
- The page tail is clamped.

At DCP > 1 that pad lands on the rank-local length, while cprr builds query positions from `g_kv_indptr`, which holds the unpadded global length. Real token t then sits at global position `S - W + t` instead of `S - q + t`, and loses `W - q` causal tokens, its own included.

**Right-align instead.** At DCP > 1 the admitted tokens are written into rows `W - q .. W - 1` of their block (`_fill_varlen_rows`). The routes then line up without touching any length:
- **cprr:** block row i sits at global position `G - W + i`. cprr derives a request's query positions from its `qo_indptr` width and its global length, so real token t lands on `S - q + t` exactly.
- **Segmented / Triton row view:** row t covers global positions `[0, S - W + t]`, which gives the same windows.
- **Pad rows:** they sit at earlier positions and only read pages the request already owns. `varlen_o_rows` drops their outputs.

At DCP1 right-alignment faulted the ASM kernel on contexts shorter than the block. That was because the plain kernel trims the block's causal tail against the local end, which cprr does not do. The GPU numerics cover sequences shorter than the block and than DCP.

**Empty shards.** For a request with nothing on a rank, the cprr kernel leaves the LSE unspecified (finite or NaN). As in uniform DCP verify, the combine masks those rows via `seq_lens == 0`, and `correct_attn_out` zeroes zero-weight partials. The numerics test now runs the merge through this production path.

**Fail early.** `_adaptive_dcp_verify_unsupported_reason` rejects these configurations:
- `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size != 1`;
- no route that places queries by global position: cprr needs gfx950, `W >= 3`, and the env not forced to `segmented`; otherwise segmented MLA or gfx942 Triton is required.

`AiterMLABackend.validate_configuration` raises with that reason rather than returning it. No other ROCm MLA backend supports AV under DCP. Without the raise, auto-selection falls back to `TRITON_MLA`, and that fails in the AV manager only after the weight load.

**Limitations**
- **#62769 is required.** At DCP > 1 the DCP group is the TP group. Each rank computes its own draft budget and per-request split, and the q head gather, the LSE merge and the round-robin KV writes all assume every rank uses the same split. Without consensus, a divergence is silently wrong output, not a hang. This exposure already exists for TP > 1 at DCP1 through the o_proj all-reduce; DCP adds the attention collectives to it.
- **Performance.** At DCP8 every batch still runs `num_reqs × W` attention rows, so AV saves only the MoE, GEMM, KDA and collective work on trimmed tokens. Performance data will come with the end-to-end run.
- **Not covered by tests:** FULL-graph replay of ragged splits at a fixed captured size, the gfx942 Triton row view, and W = 2 (segmented only). The GPU numerics run in the same CI step as the existing cprr numerics.
